title.zh: 卷二 本紀第二: 太宗上
title.raw: 卷二 本紀第二: 太宗上 Volume 2 Annals 2: Taizong 1

sentences.zh: 太宗上太宗文武大聖大廣孝皇帝諱世民，高祖第二子也。

translations.literal: Taizong, Part One: Taizong, Emperor Wenwu the Great Sage, Greatly Broad and Filial, bore the taboo personal name Shimin; he was Gaozu's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, Part One. Taizong, posthumously styled Emperor Wenwu the Great Sage, Greatly Broad and Filial, bore the taboo name Shimin and was Gaozu's second son.

sentences.zh: 母曰太穆順聖皇后竇氏。

translations.literal: His mother was Empress Taimu the Shunsheng, née Dou.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Taimu the Shunsheng of the Dou clan.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇十八年十二月戊午，生於武功之別館。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, day wuwu, of the eighteenth year of Kaihuang of Sui, he was born at the detached lodge in Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu of the twelfth month in the eighteenth year of Sui Kaihuang, he was born at the detached lodge in Wugong.

sentences.zh: 時有二龍戲於館門之外，三日而去。

translations.literal: At the time two dragons sported outside the lodge gate; after three days they departed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time two dragons were seen sporting outside the lodge gate; after three days they vanished.

sentences.zh: 高祖之臨岐州，太宗時年四歲。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took up his post at Qizhou, Taizong was then four years old.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu assumed office at Qizhou, Taizong was four years old.

sentences.zh: 有書生自言善相，謁高祖曰：「公貴人也，且有貴子。

translations.literal: A scholar who styled himself skilled in physiognomy called on Gaozu and said, "Your Excellency is a man of rank, and moreover you have a noble son.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar claiming skill in physiognomy called on Gaozu and said, "Your Excellency is a man of eminent rank, and you have a son who will be still greater.

sentences.zh: 」見太宗，曰：「龍鳳之姿，天日之表，年將二十，必能濟世安民矣。

translations.literal: " Seeing Taizong, he said, "Dragon-and-phoenix bearing, a countenance like heaven and sun; when his years approach twenty, he will surely save the age and bring peace to the people.
translations.idiomatic: " When he saw Taizong, he said, "He has the bearing of dragon and phoenix and a countenance like heaven and sun. When his years approach twenty, he will surely save the realm and bring peace to the people.

sentences.zh: 」高祖懼其言洩，將殺之，忽失所在，因採「濟世安民」之義以為名焉。

translations.literal: " Gaozu feared his words would leak out and was about to kill him, but the man suddenly vanished; he therefore took the sense of "saving the age and bringing peace to the people" as his name.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu feared the prophecy would leak out and was about to have him killed, but the man vanished without trace; Gaozu therefore drew on the phrase "save the age and bring peace to the people" and gave him the name.

sentences.zh: 太宗幼聰睿，玄鑒深遠，臨機果斷，不拘小節，時人莫能測也。

translations.literal: In youth Taizong was clever and keen, with far-reaching insight; at a crisis he was resolute, heedless of small points—men of the time could not fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Taizong was clever and penetrating, with vision that ran deep; in crisis he acted with decision and scorned petty scruples—contemporaries could not take his measure.

sentences.zh: 大業末，煬帝於雁門為突厥所圍，太宗應募救援，隸屯衛將軍云定興營。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era, when Emperor Yang at Yanmen was besieged by the Turks, Taizong answered the call for relief and was attached to the camp of Garrison Guard General Yun Dingxing.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daye reign, when Emperor Yang was besieged by the Turks at Yanmen, Taizong answered the call for relief and served under Garrison Guard General Yun Dingxing.

sentences.zh: 將行，謂定興曰：「必齎旗鼓以設疑兵。

translations.literal: As he was about to march, he said to Dingxing, "You must carry banners and drums to set up a decoy force.
translations.idiomatic: Before marching, he told Dingxing, "You must bring banners and drums to stage a feint.

sentences.zh: 且始畢可汗舉國之師，敢圍天子，必以國家倉卒無援。

translations.literal: Moreover, Shibi Khagan has led the whole nation's army and dared to encircle the Son of Heaven; he must think the state has no aid in sudden peril.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi Khagan has thrown the whole nation into this campaign and dared to hem in the Son of Heaven; he surely believes the court has no sudden help at hand.

sentences.zh: 我張軍容，令數十里幡旗相續，夜則鉦鼓相應，虜必謂救兵雲集，望塵而遁矣。

translations.literal: If we display a great host, with banners and flags strung for tens of li, and at night let gongs and drums answer one another, the barbarians will surely think relief has massed in clouds and flee at the mere sight of dust.
translations.idiomatic: If we parade a vast host—banners and flags unbroken for tens of li, gongs and drums answering through the night—the enemy will take it for clouds of relief troops and flee at the first whiff of dust.

sentences.zh: 不然，彼眾我寡，悉軍來戰，必不能支矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise, with their numbers against our few, if they bring the whole army to battle, we surely cannot hold.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, outnumbered, if they throw their full strength into battle, we cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 」定興從焉。

translations.literal: " Dingxing followed this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: " Dingxing did as he advised.

sentences.zh: 師次崞縣，突厥候騎馳告始畢曰：王師大至。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Guo County, Turkic scouts galloped to tell Shibi, "The royal army has arrived in great force."
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Guo County, Turkic scouts galloped to Shibi with word that the imperial host had arrived in strength.

sentences.zh: 由是解圍而遁。

translations.literal: Thereupon the siege was lifted and they fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks thereupon broke the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及

translations.literal: When
translations.idiomatic: Later, when

sentences.zh: 高祖之守太原，太宗時年十八。

translations.literal: Gaozu was holding Taiyuan, Taizong was then eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was garrisoning Taiyuan, Taizong was eighteen.

sentences.zh: 有高陽賊帥魏刀兒，自號歷山飛。

translations.literal: There was a Gaoyang bandit chieftain, Wei Dao'er, who styled himself Lishan Fei.
translations.idiomatic: A Gaoyang bandit chieftain, Wei Dao'er, styled himself Lishan Fei.

sentences.zh: 來攻太原，高祖擊之，深入賊陣。

translations.literal: He came to attack Taiyuan; Gaozu struck back and drove deep into the rebel lines.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Taiyuan; Gaozu counterattacked and plunged deep into the rebel formation.

sentences.zh: 太宗以輕騎突圍而進，射之，所向皆披靡，拔高祖於萬眾之中。

translations.literal: Taizong with light cavalry broke through the encirclement and advanced, shooting; wherever he turned, the enemy scattered, and he pulled Gaozu from amid ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong led light cavalry through the encirclement, shooting as he charged; wherever he turned the enemy broke, and he drew Gaozu out from amid ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 適會步兵至，高祖與太宗又奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Just then the infantry arrived; Gaozu and Taizong struck again with fury and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the foot soldiers came up; Gaozu and Taizong attacked again with fury and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 時隋祚已終，太宗潛圖義舉，每折節下士，推財養客，群盜大俠，莫不願效死力。

translations.literal: By then the Sui mandate was spent; Taizong secretly plotted a righteous rising. He humbled himself to win scholars, spent wealth to keep clients—great bandits and wandering swordsmen all wished to die for him.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui mandate was already spent; Taizong secretly planned a righteous uprising. He lowered himself to win men of talent, spent his wealth to keep clients—outlaws and wandering champions alike were ready to die for him.

sentences.zh: 及義兵起，乃率兵略徇西河，克之。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, he led troops to seize and subdue Xihe and took it.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose, he led troops to overrun Xihe and captured it.

sentences.zh: 拜右領大都督，右三軍皆隸焉，封燉煌郡公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Army Commander-in-chief; the three right armies were all placed under him, and he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Army Commander-in-chief, with all three right armies under his command, and enfeoffed as Duke of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 大軍西上賈胡堡，隋將宋老生率精兵二萬屯霍邑，以拒義師。

translations.literal: As the main army marched west to Jiahu Fort, Sui general Song Laosheng led twenty thousand picked troops to camp at Huoyi and block the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: As the main host marched west toward Jiahu Fort, Sui general Song Laosheng led twenty thousand elite troops to Huoyi to block the righteous army.

sentences.zh: 會久雨糧盡，高祖與裴寂議，且還太原，以圖後舉。

translations.literal: Prolonged rain had exhausted the grain; Gaozu and Pei Ji debated withdrawing to Taiyuan to plan another attempt.
translations.idiomatic: Endless rain had exhausted their grain; Gaozu and Pei Ji debated falling back to Taiyuan to try again later.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「本興大義以救蒼生，當須先入咸陽，號令天下；

translations.literal: Taizong said, "We raised a great cause to save the black-haired people; we must first enter Xianyang and command the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "We took up arms to save the people; we must first enter Xianyang and command the realm.

sentences.zh: 遇小敵即班師，將恐從義之徒一朝解體。

translations.literal: if at the first small enemy we turn back, I fear those who joined the cause will dissolve in a morning.
translations.idiomatic: If we retreat at the first small foe, those who joined us will scatter overnight.

sentences.zh: 還守太原一城之地，此為賊耳，何以自全！

translations.literal: To hold only the ground of Taiyuan city makes us mere bandits—how can we preserve ourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Holding one city at Taiyuan would make us nothing but bandits—how could we survive?"

sentences.zh: 」高祖不納，促令引發。

translations.literal: " Gaozu did not accept this and urgently ordered the army to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu would not listen and ordered a prompt withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 太宗遂號泣於外，聲聞帳中。

translations.literal: Taizong then wept aloud outside the tent until the sound reached within.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wept outside the tent until his voice carried inside.

sentences.zh: 高祖召問其故，對曰：「今兵以義動，進戰則必克，退還則必散。

translations.literal: Gaozu summoned him and asked why; he replied, "Now the army moves on righteousness; if we advance we are sure to win, if we retreat we are sure to scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu called him in and asked why; he answered, "The army marches on righteousness now—advance and we win, retreat and we scatter.

sentences.zh: 眾散於前，敵乘於後，死亡須臾而至，是以悲耳。

translations.literal: The host scatters before us and the enemy presses from behind—death comes in an instant; that is why I grieve."
translations.idiomatic: Our men will break before us and the enemy will strike from behind—death in an instant. That is why I weep."

sentences.zh: 」高祖乃悟而止。

translations.literal: " Gaozu then understood and halted.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu understood and called off the retreat.

sentences.zh: 八月己卯，雨霽，高祖引師趣霍邑。

translations.literal: On jimao of the eighth month the rain cleared; Gaozu led the army toward Huoyi.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao of the eighth month the skies cleared; Gaozu marched on Huoyi.

sentences.zh: 太宗恐老生不出戰，乃將數騎先詣其城下，舉鞭指麾，若將圍城者，以激怒之。

translations.literal: Taizong feared Laosheng would not come out to fight; he took several horsemen ahead to the foot of the wall, raised his whip and gestured as if to invest the city, to provoke him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Laosheng would not sally forth, Taizong rode ahead with a few horsemen to the wall, gestured with his whip as though to invest the city, and goaded him into battle.

sentences.zh: 老生果怒，開門出兵，背城而陣。

translations.literal: Laosheng was indeed enraged, opened the gate and sent out troops, and drew up his battle line with his back to the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Laosheng took the bait, opened the gates, and formed his line with the wall at his back.

sentences.zh: 高祖與建成合陣於城東，太宗及柴紹陣於城南。

translations.literal: Gaozu and Jiancheng joined battle lines east of the city; Taizong and Chai Shao formed lines south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu and Jiancheng drew up east of the city; Taizong and Chai Shao south of it.

sentences.zh: 老生麾兵疾進，先薄高祖，而建成墜馬，老生乘之，高祖與建成軍咸卻。

translations.literal: Laosheng waved his troops forward in haste; they first pressed Gaozu, and Jiancheng fell from his horse; Laosheng seized the chance—Gaozu's and Jiancheng's forces all fell back.
translations.idiomatic: Laosheng drove his men forward; they first bore down on Gaozu. Jiancheng was thrown from his horse, and Laosheng pressed the advantage—Gaozu's and Jiancheng's lines gave way.

sentences.zh: 太宗自南原率二騎馳下峻阪，沖斷其軍，引兵奮擊，賊眾大敗，各舍仗而走。

translations.literal: Taizong from the southern heights led two horsemen charging down the steep slope, cut through the enemy army, led his troops in fierce attack, and the rebels were utterly routed, each casting aside weapons and fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong swept down the southern heights with two horsemen, smashed through the enemy line, and led a furious charge; the rebels broke completely, casting aside weapons as they fled.

sentences.zh: 懸門發，老生引繩欲上，遂斬之，平霍邑。

translations.literal: The drawbridge was raised; Laosheng tried to haul himself up by rope, but was beheaded; Huoyi was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The drawbridge rose; Laosheng tried to climb the rope but was cut down; Huoyi fell.

sentences.zh: 至河東，關中豪傑爭走赴義。

translations.literal: Reaching the east of the River, the bold men of Guanzhong vied to join the cause.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the east of the River, Guanzhong's champions hurried to the cause.

sentences.zh: 太宗請進師入關，取永豐倉以賑窮乏，收群盜以圖京師，高祖稱善。

translations.literal: Taizong asked to advance into the Pass, take Yongfeng Granary to relieve the destitute, gather the bandits to aim at the capital—Gaozu praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong asked leave to enter the Pass, seize Yongfeng Granary to feed the hungry, and rally the outlaws against the capital; Gaozu approved.

sentences.zh: 太宗以前軍濟河，先定渭北。

translations.literal: Taizong with the vanguard crossed the river and first secured the north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong crossed first with the vanguard and secured the north bank of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 三輔吏民及諸豪猾詣軍門請自效者日以千計，扶老攜幼，滿於麾下。

translations.literal: Officials and people of the Three Adjuncts and all manner of local strongmen who came to the camp gate to offer service numbered thousands a day; old and young filled his command.
translations.idiomatic: Each day thousands of officials, commoners, and local strongmen of the Three Adjuncts came to his gate to serve—old and young crowding under his banner.

sentences.zh: 收納英俊，以備僚列，遠近聞者，咸自托焉。

translations.literal: He gathered outstanding men to fill his staff; those who heard of him from afar all entrusted themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered able men for his staff; all who heard of him from afar came to his side.

sentences.zh: 師次於涇陽，勝兵九萬，破胡賊劉鷂子，並其眾。

translations.literal: The army halted at Jingyang with ninety thousand effectives, defeated the Hu bandit Liu Yaozi, and absorbed his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Halting at Jingyang with ninety thousand fighting men, he defeated the Hu bandit Liu Yaozi and took his force into his own.

sentences.zh: 留殷開山、劉弘基屯長安故城。

translations.literal: He left Yin Kaishan and Liu Hongji to garrison the old city of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He left Yin Kaishan and Liu Hongji to hold the old walls of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 太宗自趣司竹，賊帥李仲文、何潘仁、向善志等皆來會，頓於阿城，獲兵十三萬。

translations.literal: Taizong himself pressed on to Sizhu; bandit chiefs Li Zhongwen, He Panren, Xiang Shanzi, and others all came to join him. He encamped at Acheng and gathered a hundred and thirty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong pressed on to Sizhu; bandit chiefs Li Zhongwen, He Panren, Xiang Shanzi, and others joined him. He camped at Acheng with a hundred and thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 長安父老齎牛酒詣旌門者不可勝紀，勞而遣之，一無所受。

translations.literal: Chang'an elders who brought oxen and wine to his standard gate could not be counted; he thanked them and sent them away, accepting nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Countless Chang'an elders brought oxen and wine to his camp; he thanked them and sent them away, taking nothing.

sentences.zh: 軍令嚴肅，秋毫無所犯。

translations.literal: Army discipline was stern; not the slightest thing was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline was iron; not a hair of the people was touched.

sentences.zh: 尋與大軍平京城。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he joined the main army in pacifying the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined the main host in taking the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖輔政，受唐國內史，改封秦國公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu served as regent, Taizong received the post of Director of the Secretariat for the State of Tang and was transferred to Duke of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu acted as regent, Taizong became Director of the Secretariat for the State of Tang and was raised to Duke of Qin.

sentences.zh: 會薛舉以勁卒十萬來逼渭濱，太宗親擊之，大破其眾，追斬萬餘級，略地至於隴坻。

translations.literal: When Xue Ju came with a hundred thousand crack troops to press the Wei shore, Taizong met him in person, routed his host, pursued and slew more than ten thousand, and carried the frontier to Longdi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Ju brought a hundred thousand crack troops to the Wei, Taizong met him in person, shattered his army, cut down more than ten thousand in pursuit, and carried the frontier to Longdi.

sentences.zh: 義寧元年十二月，復為右元帥，總兵十萬徇東都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Yining, he was again made Right Grand Marshal and commanded a hundred thousand troops to overrun the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Yining 1 he was again Right Grand Marshal, commanding a hundred thousand men against the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 及將旋，謂左右曰：「賊見吾還，必相追躡。

translations.literal: As he was about to turn back, he told those beside him, "When the rebels see us return, they will surely pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Before turning back he told his staff, "When the enemy sees us withdraw, they will surely give chase.

sentences.zh: 」設三伏以待之。

translations.literal: " He set three ambushes to await them.
translations.idiomatic: " He laid three ambushes to receive them.

sentences.zh: 俄而隋將段達率萬餘人自後而至，度三王陵，發伏擊之，段達大敗，追奔至於城下。

translations.literal: Before long Sui general Duan Da led more than ten thousand men up from the rear; when they reached Sanwang Mound the ambush struck and Da was utterly defeated; the pursuit ran to the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Sui general Duan Da came from behind with more than ten thousand men; at Sanwang Mound the ambush sprang and Da was shattered; pursuit carried to the walls.

sentences.zh: 因於宜陽、新安置熊、穀二州，戍之而還。

translations.literal: He then established the two prefectures of Xiong and Gu in Yiyang and Xin'an and garrisoned them before returning.
translations.idiomatic: He then set up the prefectures of Xiong and Gu at Yiyang and Xin'an, left garrisons, and returned.

sentences.zh: 徙封趙國公。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜尚書令、右武候大將軍，進封秦王，加授雍州牧。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Taizong was appointed Director of the Secretariat and Right Martial Guard Grand General; he was advanced to Prince of Qin and additionally made Governor of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Taizong became Director of the Secretariat and Right Martial Guard Grand General, was advanced to Prince of Qin, and made Governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 武德元年七月，薛舉寇涇州，太宗率眾討之，不利而旋。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Wude, Xue Ju raided Jing Prefecture; Taizong led troops against him, met ill fortune, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Wude 1, Xue Ju raided Jing Prefecture; Taizong marched against him, fared badly, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 九月，薛舉死，其子仁杲嗣立。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Xue Ju died; his son Rengao succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Xue Ju died; his son Rengao took his place.

sentences.zh: 太宗又為元帥以擊仁杲，相持於折墌城，深溝高壘者六十餘日。

translations.literal: Taizong was again made Grand Marshal to strike Rengao; they faced each other at Zheyu Fort for more than sixty days behind deep ditches and high ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was again Grand Marshal against Rengao; for more than sixty days they faced each other at Zheyu behind deep trenches and high walls.

sentences.zh: 賊眾十餘萬，兵鋒甚銳，數來挑戰，太宗按甲以挫之。

translations.literal: The rebel host numbered more than a hundred thousand; their edge was keen and they came repeatedly to offer battle; Taizong held his armor to wear them down.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels numbered more than a hundred thousand, keen and bold, challenging battle again and again; Taizong kept his men under cover to break their spirit.

sentences.zh: 賊糧盡，其將牟君才、梁胡郎來降。

translations.literal: When the rebels' grain was spent, their generals Mou Jun'ai and Liang Hulang came over.
translations.idiomatic: When their grain ran out, generals Mou Jun'ai and Liang Hulang defected.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂諸將軍曰：「彼氣衰矣，吾當取之。

translations.literal: Taizong told the generals, "Their spirit is spent; I shall take them."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told his commanders, "Their spirit is broken; I will finish them."

sentences.zh: 」遣將軍龐玉先陣於淺水原南以誘之，賊將宗羅㬋並軍來拒，玉軍幾敗。

translations.literal: " He sent General Pang Yu to form a line south of Qianshui Plain to lure them; rebel general Zong Luohou joined his whole army to resist, and Yu's force nearly collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Pang Yu to draw them on south of Qianshui Plain; rebel general Zong Luohou brought his full host to meet him, and Yu nearly broke.

sentences.zh: 既而太宗親御大軍，奄自原北，出其不意。

translations.literal: Then Taizong personally led the main army, sweeping down from the north of the plain to take them unawares.
translations.idiomatic: Then Taizong led the main host himself, sweeping from the north of the plain to strike where they did not expect.

sentences.zh: 羅㬋望見，復回師相拒。

translations.literal: When Luohou saw this, he wheeled his army back to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou saw him and turned back to meet the blow.

sentences.zh: 太宗將驍騎數十入賊陣，於是王師表裏齊奮，羅㬋大潰，斬首數千級，投澗穀而死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: Taizong led several dozen of his finest horsemen into the rebel lines; then the royal army struck from within and without together—Luohou was utterly routed, several thousand heads were taken, and those who plunged into ravines and gullies could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong plunged in with several dozen of his finest horsemen; the imperial line struck from every side at once. Luohou's host collapsed; thousands were slain, and the dead choked the ravines beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 太宗率左右二十餘騎追奔，直趣折墌以乘之。

translations.literal: Taizong with some twenty horsemen at his side pursued the rout straight to Zheyu to press the advantage.
translations.idiomatic: With barely twenty horsemen at his side, Taizong chased the rout straight to Zheyu to press the kill.

sentences.zh: 仁杲大懼，嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Rengao was greatly afraid and shut himself in the city to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Rengao was terrified and walled himself in.

sentences.zh: 將夕，大軍繼至，四面合圍。

translations.literal: Toward evening the main army came up and invested the city on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: By evening the main host arrived and ringed the city.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，仁杲請降，俘其精兵萬餘人、男女五萬口。

translations.literal: At dawn Rengao asked to surrender; they captured more than ten thousand of his crack troops and fifty thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Rengao surrendered; they took more than ten thousand of his best troops and fifty thousand men and women captive.

sentences.zh: 既而諸將奉賀，因問曰：「始大王野戰破賊，其主尚保堅城，王無攻具，輕騎騰逐，不待步兵，徑薄城下，咸疑不克，而竟下之，何也？

translations.literal: Then the generals offered congratulations and asked, "At first Your Highness broke the rebels in field battle, yet their lord still held a stout city; Your Highness had no siege engines, yet with light cavalry you galloped in pursuit, not waiting for the foot soldiers, and pressed straight to the wall—all doubted you could take it, yet you did. Why?"
translations.idiomatic: The generals then congratulated him and asked, "Your Highness shattered them in the field, yet their lord still held a strong city; you had no engines of siege, yet with light horse you raced in pursuit without waiting for the foot, and pressed straight to the walls—we doubted you could take it, yet you did. How?"

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「此以權道迫之，使其計不暇發，以故克也。

translations.literal: Taizong said, "This was to press them by expedient so their plans had no time to form; that is why we took it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "I pressed them by stratagem so their plans never had time to form—that is how we took it.

sentences.zh: 羅㬋恃往年之勝，兼復養銳日久，見吾不出，意在相輕。

translations.literal: Luohou relied on victories in former years and had long been sharpening his edge; seeing that we did not come out, he meant to hold us cheap.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou trusted his old victories and had long been resting on his steel; seeing us hold back, he thought little of us.

sentences.zh: 今喜吾出，悉兵來戰，雖擊破之，擒殺蓋少。

translations.literal: Now, pleased that we had come out, he brought his whole army to battle; though we broke them, captures and kills were still few.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw us advance, he threw his whole strength into battle; though we broke him, few were killed or taken.

sentences.zh: 若不急躡，還走投城，仁杲收而撫之，則便未可得矣。

translations.literal: If we did not press the pursuit at once and they fled back to the city for Rengao to gather and comfort them, we could not have had them so soon.
translations.idiomatic: Had we not pressed hard at once, they would have fled back to the city for Rengao to rally and steady them, and the prize would have slipped away.

sentences.zh: 且其兵眾皆隴西人，一敗披退，不及回顧，散歸隴外，則折墌自虛，我軍隨而迫之，所以懼而降也。

translations.literal: Moreover, his soldiers were all men of Longxi; once beaten they would scatter in flight without looking back, drifting beyond Long; then Zheyu would stand empty, and as our army pressed close behind, that is why he was afraid and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: And his men were Longxi men—once broken they would flee without a backward glance, scattering beyond Long, leaving Zheyu empty; our host pressed on their heels, and that is why he surrendered in fear.

sentences.zh: 此可謂成算，諸君盡不見耶？

translations.literal: This was a settled plan—did you all not see it?"
translations.idiomatic: It was a settled plan—did none of you see it?"

sentences.zh: 」諸將曰：「此非凡人所能及也。

translations.literal: " The generals said, "This is beyond what an ordinary man could reach."
translations.idiomatic: " The generals said, "No ordinary man could have done this."

sentences.zh: 」獲賊兵精騎甚眾，還令仁杲兄弟及賊帥宗羅㬋、翟長孫等領之。

translations.literal: " They had taken many of the rebels' finest horsemen; Taizong sent Rengao's brothers and the rebel chiefs Zong Luohou, Zhai Changsun, and others to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: " They had taken many of the enemy's best horse; Taizong put Rengao's brothers and chiefs Zong Luohou, Zhai Changsun, and others in command of them.

sentences.zh: 太宗與之游獵馳射，無所間然。

translations.literal: Taizong hunted and shot with them in the open field without the least reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong rode to hunt and shoot with them in the open without reserve.

sentences.zh: 賊徒荷恩懾氣，咸願效死。

translations.literal: The rebels, grateful and awed, all wished to die for him.
translations.idiomatic: Bound by gratitude and fear, the captives were ready to die for him.

sentences.zh: 時李密初附，高祖令密馳傳迎太宗於豳州。

translations.literal: At that time Li Mi had just submitted; Gaozu ordered Mi to dispatch a fast courier to welcome Taizong at Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi had just submitted; Gaozu sent him with a fast courier to welcome Taizong at Bin.

sentences.zh: 密見太宗天姿神武，軍威嚴肅，驚悚嘆服，私謂殷開山曰：「真英主也。

translations.literal: Mi saw Taizong's heaven-sent bearing and stern military majesty, was startled and sighed in admiration, and privately told Yin Kaishan, "A true hero-emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Mi saw Taizong's bearing—heaven-sent, his host iron-disciplined—and was shaken to admiration; privately he told Yin Kaishan, "This is a true hero-emperor.

sentences.zh: 不如此，何以定禍亂乎？

translations.literal: Were he not such, how could the age's calamities be settled?"
translations.idiomatic: Without such a man, how could this chaos ever be stilled?"

sentences.zh: 」凱旋，獻捷於太廟。

translations.literal: " Returning in triumph, he presented the victory at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: " On his triumphant return he reported victory at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 拜太尉、陜東道行臺尚書令，鎮長春宮，關東兵馬並受節度。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Commandant, Director of the Secretariat for the Shaan-dong Circuit, garrisoned Changchun Palace, and all troops east of the Pass were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Commandant and Director of the Secretariat for the Shaan-dong Circuit, garrisoned Changchun Palace, and all armies east of the Pass answered to him.

sentences.zh: 尋加左武候大將軍、涼州總管。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Left Martial Guard Grand General and Overall Commander of Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also Left Martial Guard Grand General and Overall Commander of Liang.

sentences.zh: 宋金剛之陷澮州也，兵鋒甚銳。

translations.literal: When Song Jingang took Fen Prefecture, his military edge was keen.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Jingang seized Fen Prefecture, his armies were at their sharpest.

sentences.zh: 高祖以王行本尚據蒲州，呂崇茂反於夏縣，晉、澮二州相繼陷沒，關中震駭，乃手敕曰：「賊勢如此，難與爭鋒，宜棄河東之地，謹守關西而已。

translations.literal: Gaozu, with Wang Xingben still holding Pu Prefecture and Lü Chongmao in revolt at Xia County, with Jin and Fen falling in turn and Guanzhong shaken, wrote in his own hand: "The rebels' power is such that it is hard to meet their edge; we should abandon the lands east of the River and guard only the Pass west."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingben still held Pu, Lü Chongmao had risen at Xia, Jin and Fen had fallen in turn, and Guanzhong trembled; Gaozu wrote in his own hand, "The enemy is too strong to meet head-on—we should yield the east of the River and hold only the west of the Pass."

sentences.zh: 」太宗上表曰：「太原王業所基，國之根本，河東殷實，京邑所資。

translations.literal: Taizong memorialized: "Taiyuan is the base of the royal enterprise, the root of the state; Hedong is rich and solid, the sustenance of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong memorialized, "Taiyuan is where our house was founded, the root of the realm; Hedong is rich and feeds the capital.

sentences.zh: 若舉而棄之，臣竊憤恨。

translations.literal: To raise it up and then cast it away—I, your servant, burn with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: To win it and then throw it away—I cannot bear the thought.

sentences.zh: 願假精兵三萬，必能平殄武周，克復汾、晉。

translations.literal: I beg for thirty thousand picked troops; I will surely destroy Wu Zhou and recover Fen and Jin."
translations.idiomatic: Give me thirty thousand picked men, and I will destroy Wu Zhou and win back Fen and Jin."

sentences.zh: 」高祖於是悉發關中兵以益之，又幸長春宮親送太宗。

translations.literal: Gaozu thereupon sent out all the troops of Guanzhong to reinforce him, and in person went to Changchun Palace to see Taizong off.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then sent every soldier Guanzhong could spare to strengthen him, and went in person to Changchun Palace to see him off.

sentences.zh: 二年十一月，太宗率眾趣龍門關，履冰而渡之，進屯柏壁，與賊將宋金剛相持。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year, Taizong led his army toward Longmen Pass, crossed on the ice, and encamped at Baibi, where he faced the rebel general Song Jingang in a stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Wude 2 Taizong marched on Longmen Pass, crossed the frozen river, and camped at Baibi to hold Song Jingang at bay.

sentences.zh: 尋而永安王孝基敗於夏縣，於筠、獨孤懷恩、唐儉並為賊將尋相、尉遲敬德所執，將還澮州。

translations.literal: Before long Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji was defeated at Xia County; Yu Jun, Dugu Huai'en, and Tang Jian were all seized by the rebel generals Xun Xiang and Yuchi Jingde and were being taken back to Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji was beaten at Xia County; Yu Jun, Dugu Huai'en, and Tang Jian fell into the hands of Xun Xiang and Yuchi Jingde and were marched toward Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣殷開山、秦叔寶邀之於美良川，大破之，相等僅以身免，悉虜其眾，復歸柏壁。

translations.literal: Taizong sent Yin Kaishan and Qin Shubao to intercept them on the Meiliang River, routed them utterly, and Xiang and the rest barely escaped with their lives; he took the whole force captive and returned to Baibi.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent Yin Kaishan and Qin Shubao to ambush them on the Meiliang River, crushed the column, and captured the lot; Xiang alone slipped away. The army then returned to Baibi.

sentences.zh: 於是諸將咸請戰，太宗曰：「金剛懸軍千里，深入吾地，精兵驍將，皆在於此。

translations.literal: Thereupon the generals all asked to give battle. Taizong said: "Jingang has hung his army a thousand li out and driven deep into our territory; his crack troops and fierce commanders are all here.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders all pressed for battle. Taizong said: "Jingang has marched a thousand li and plunged deep into our land; every elite soldier and bold captain he has is in this camp.

sentences.zh: 武周據太原，專倚金剛以為捍。

translations.literal: Wuzhou holds Taiyuan and relies on Jingang alone as his shield.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou sits in Taiyuan and trusts Jingang alone to shield him.

sentences.zh: 士卒雖眾，內實空虛，意在速戰。

translations.literal: Though their numbers are great, within they are hollow; they mean to fight quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Their host looks vast, but it is empty at the core—they want a swift decision.

sentences.zh: 我堅營蓄銳以挫其鋒，糧盡計窮，自當遁走。

translations.literal: We shall hold our camps, store our strength, and blunt their edge; when grain is gone and plans exhausted, they will flee of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: We will stand fast, husband our strength, and break their momentum; when supplies fail and schemes run dry, they will break and run without our chasing them.
[End of his reply.]

sentences.zh: 三年二月，金剛竟以眾餒而遁，太宗追之至介州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year Jingang at last fled with his starving troops; Taizong pursued him to Jie Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Wude 3 Jingang finally broke away with a starving army; Taizong chased him to Jie Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 金剛列陣，南北七里，以拒官軍。

translations.literal: Jingang drew up his battle line seven li from north to south to block the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Jingang formed a line seven li long from north to south to meet the Tang forces.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣總管李世勣、程咬金、秦叔寶當其北，翟長孫、秦武通當其南。

translations.literal: Taizong sent Supervisors Li Shiji, Cheng Yaojin, and Qin Shubao to face the north; Zhai Zhangsun and Qin Wutong the south.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong posted Li Shiji, Cheng Yaojin, and Qin Shubao on the north; Zhai Zhangsun and Qin Wutong on the south.

sentences.zh: 諸軍戰小卻，為賊所乘。

translations.literal: The armies gave a little ground in the fighting and were taken advantage of by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang lines buckled slightly and the rebels pressed the advantage.

sentences.zh: 太宗率精騎擊之，沖其陣後，賊眾大敗，追奔數十里。

translations.literal: Taizong led his elite cavalry to strike them, charged through to the rear of their formation, and the rebel host was utterly broken; the pursuit ran for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong himself led the elite horse, hit their rear, and shattered them; the pursuit carried tens of li.

sentences.zh: 敬德、相率眾八千來降，還令敬德督之，與軍營相參。

translations.literal: Jingde and Xiang led eight thousand men to surrender; Taizong again had Jingde command them, intermingled with the camps.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde and Xiang brought eight thousand men over; Taizong put Jingde in charge of them, mixed in among his own units.

sentences.zh: 屈突通懼其為變，驟以為請。

translations.literal: Qu Tu Tong, fearing they would turn traitor, urgently petitioned on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tu Tong, fearing treachery, urgently asked that they be disarmed or removed.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「昔蕭王推赤心置人腹中，並能畢命，今委任敬德，又何疑也。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "In old times the Duke of Xiao laid his open heart in another's breast, and men gave their lives to the end; now that I entrust Jingde, what is there to doubt?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "Long ago the Duke of Xiao trusted men with his whole heart, and they died for him without reserve. Jingde has my trust—why should I doubt him?

sentences.zh: 」於是劉武周奔於突厥，並、汾悉復舊地。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Liu Wuzhou fled to the Turks, and Bing and Fen were all restored to the old boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou fled to the Turks; Bing and Fen were recovered in full.

sentences.zh: 詔就軍加拜益州道行臺尚書令。

translations.literal: An edict promoted him on the spot to Chief Minister of the Yizhou Circuit headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he was promoted in the field to Chief Minister of the Yizhou Circuit headquarters.

sentences.zh: 七月，總率諸軍攻王世充於洛邑，師次穀州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he took overall command of the armies attacking Wang Shichong at Luoyang and halted at Gu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he took supreme command against Wang Shichong at Luoyang and encamped at Gu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世充率精兵三萬陣於慈澗，太宗以輕騎挑之。

translations.literal: Shichong led thirty thousand picked troops and drew up at Ciyong Stream; Taizong provoked him with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong brought thirty thousand elite troops to Ciyong Stream; Taizong baited him with a light horse screen.

sentences.zh: 時眾寡不敵，陷於重圍，左右咸懼。

translations.literal: At the time they were badly outnumbered and fell into a tight encirclement; those about him were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, he was hemmed in; even his attendants feared the worst.

sentences.zh: 太宗命左右先歸，獨留後殿。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered those at his side to withdraw first and alone brought up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent his companions ahead and alone covered the retreat.

sentences.zh: 世充驍將單雄信數百騎夾道來逼，交搶競進，太宗幾為所敗。

translations.literal: Shichong's fierce general Shan Xiongxin with several hundred horsemen came pressing along both sides of the road, spears crossing as they vied forward; Taizong was nearly undone.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Xiongxin, Shichong's boldest captain, closed in with hundreds of horse along the road; Taizong came within a hair of defeat.

sentences.zh: 太宗左右射之，無不應弦而倒，獲其大將燕頎。

translations.literal: Taizong shot left and right; none failed to fall at the twang of the bowstring, and he took their great general Yan Xie.
translations.idiomatic: He shot to either flank; every arrow found its mark, and he captured the great general Yan Xie.

sentences.zh: 世充乃拔慈澗之鎮歸於東都。

translations.literal: Shichong thereupon abandoned the Ciyong garrison and withdrew to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong then abandoned the Ciyong strongpoint and pulled back to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣行軍總管史萬寶自宜陽南據龍門，劉德威自太行東圍河內，王君廓自洛口斷賊糧道。

translations.literal: Taizong sent Campaign General Shi Wanbao from the south of Yiyang to hold Longmen, Liu Dewei from the east of the Taihang range to invest Henei, and Wang Junkuo from Luokou to sever the rebel grain route.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Shi Wanbao south from Yiyang to seize Longmen, Liu Dewei east of the Taihang to besiege Henei, and Wang Junkuo from Luokou to cut Shichong's supply line.

sentences.zh: 又遣黃君漢夜從孝水河中下舟師襲回洛城，克之。

translations.literal: He also sent Huang Junhan by night to float boats down the Xiaoshui and strike Huiluo city, which was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Junhan was sent by night down the Xiaoshui with a fleet to storm Huiluo city and took it.

sentences.zh: 黃河已南，莫不響應，城堡相次來降。

translations.literal: South of the Yellow River none failed to answer the call; fortresses and walled towns surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yellow River the country rose in answer; strongpoints surrendered in succession.

sentences.zh: 大軍進屯邙山。

translations.literal: The main army advanced and encamped on Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: The main force moved up and camped on Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 九月，太宗以五百騎先觀戰地，卒與世充萬餘人相遇，會戰，復破之，斬首三千餘級，獲大將陳智略，世充僅以身免。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Taizong with five hundred horsemen went ahead to reconnoiter the field and suddenly met more than ten thousand of Shichong's men; they joined battle, broke them again, beheaded more than three thousand, took the great general Chen Zhilue, and Shichong barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, scouting with five hundred horse, he stumbled on more than ten thousand of Shichong's troops, routed them, took three thousand heads and the general Chen Zhilue, and Shichong fled alone.

sentences.zh: 其所署筠州總管楊慶遣使請降，遣李世勣率師出轘轅道安撫其眾。

translations.literal: Yang Qing, whom Shichong had appointed commander of Yun Prefecture, sent envoys to offer surrender; Taizong sent Li Shiji with troops out by the Xuanyuan Pass road to pacify his following.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing, Shichong's commander at Yun Prefecture, sent envoys to submit; Taizong sent Li Shiji by the Xuanyuan road to bring his troops over.

sentences.zh: 滎、汴、洧、豫九州相繼來降。

translations.literal: The nine prefectures of Xing, Bian, Wei, and Yu surrendered in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Xing, Bian, Wei, and Yu—the nine prefectures of the region—came over one after another.

sentences.zh: 世充遂求救於竇建德。

translations.literal: Shichong then begged Dou Jiande for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong turned to Dou Jiande for aid.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，又進屯青城宮。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year he again advanced and encamped at Qingcheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Wude 4 he moved forward again to Qingcheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 營壘未立，世充眾二萬自方諸門臨谷水而陣。

translations.literal: Before the ramparts were finished, twenty thousand of Shichong's men came from Fangzhu Gate and drew up along the valley water.
translations.idiomatic: Before the camp was complete, twenty thousand of Shichong's troops issued from Fangzhu Gate and formed along the stream.

sentences.zh: 太宗以精騎陣於北邙山，令屈突通率步卒五千渡水以擊之，因誡通曰：「待兵交即放煙，吾當率騎軍南下。

translations.literal: Taizong arrayed his elite cavalry on Mount Mang to the north and ordered Qu Tu Tong with five thousand foot soldiers to cross the water and strike them, charging him: "When the infantry clash, set off smoke; I shall lead the cavalry south.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong lined his elite horse on the northern slope of Mount Mang and ordered Qu Tu Tong with five thousand foot to cross and attack, telling him: "The moment the foot engage, light the signal—I will come down with the cavalry."

sentences.zh: 」兵才接，太宗以騎沖之，挺身先進，與通表裏相應。

translations.literal: " As soon as the lines met, Taizong charged with his cavalry, thrust himself forward at the head, and coordinated with Tong inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: The instant the armies met, Taizong drove in with his horse, took the lead himself, and struck in concert with Tong from both sides.

sentences.zh: 賊眾殊死戰，散而復合者數焉。

translations.literal: The rebel host fought to the death; they scattered and re-formed several times.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fought with desperate fury, breaking and re-forming again and again.

sentences.zh: 自辰及午，賊眾始退。

translations.literal: From the hour chen until wu the rebel lines at last gave way.
translations.idiomatic: From mid-morning until noon the enemy line finally broke.

sentences.zh: 縱兵乘之，俘斬八千人，於是進營城下。

translations.literal: He loosed his troops in pursuit; more than eight thousand were captured or slain, and he then advanced and encamped beneath the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the army in pursuit; eight thousand were killed or taken, then he pitched camp under the city walls.

sentences.zh: 世充不敢復出，但嬰城自守，以待建德之援。

translations.literal: Shichong dared not come out again but clung to the walls and waited for Jiande's relief.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong would not sally again; he held the walls and waited for Jiande.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣諸軍掘塹，匝布長圍以守之。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered the armies to dig trenches and ring the city in a long encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had trenches dug and a full cordon drawn round the city.

sentences.zh: 吳王杜伏威遣其將陳正通、徐召宗率精兵二千來會於軍所。

translations.literal: Prince of Wu Du Fuwei sent his generals Chen Zhengtong and Xu Zhaozong with two thousand elite troops to join the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fuwei, Prince of Wu, sent Chen Zhengtong and Xu Zhaozong with two thousand picked men to the camp.

sentences.zh: 偽鄭州司馬沈悅以武牢降，將軍王君廓應之，擒其偽荊王王行本。

translations.literal: Shen Yue, bogus prefectural marshal of Zheng Prefecture, surrendered Hulao; General Wang Junkuo answered him and captured the bogus Prince of Jing Wang Xingben.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue, Shichong's marshal at Zheng Prefecture, surrendered Hulao; Wang Junkuo moved up and seized the bogus Prince of Jing, Wang Xingben.

sentences.zh: 會竇建德以兵十餘萬來援世充，至於酸棗。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande came with more than a hundred thousand men to relieve Shichong and reached Suanzao.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande marched to Shichong's aid with more than a hundred thousand men and reached Suanzao.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀、屈突通、封德彞皆以腹背受敵，恐非萬全，請退師穀州以觀之。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu, Qu Tu Tong, and Feng Deyi all said that with enemies before and behind them success was not assured and asked to withdraw the army to Gu Prefecture to watch developments.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu, Qu Tu Tong, and Feng Deyi all warned that caught between Shichong and Jiande the position was perilous and urged a withdrawal to Gu Prefecture to wait.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「世充糧盡，內外離心，我當不勞攻擊，坐收其敝。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "Shichong's grain is exhausted and hearts within and without are divided; we need not labor to attack—we may sit and gather the spoil of their exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "Shichong is out of grain and his people are splitting within and without. We need not storm the walls—we can let exhaustion do our work.

sentences.zh: 建德新破孟海公，將驕卒惰，吾當進據武牢，扼其襟要。

translations.literal: Jiande has newly defeated Meng Haigong; his generals are proud and his soldiers slack—we should advance and seize Hulao, choking their throat.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande has just crushed Meng Haigong; his officers are arrogant and his men lax. We should seize Hulao and grip him by the throat.

sentences.zh: 賊若冒險與我爭鋒，破之必矣。

translations.literal: If the enemy dare meet us in a pitched fight, we are sure to break them.
translations.idiomatic: If they dare meet us in the open, we will break them.

sentences.zh: 如其不戰，旬日間世充當自潰。

translations.literal: If they will not fight, within ten days Shichong will collapse of himself.
translations.idiomatic: If they refuse battle, Shichong will fall apart within ten days.

sentences.zh: 若不速進，賊入武牢，諸城新附，必不能守。

translations.literal: If we do not advance quickly and the enemy enters Hulao, the cities newly submitted cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: If we delay and Jiande takes Hulao, every city that just submitted will slip from our grasp.

sentences.zh: 二賊並力，將若之何？

translations.literal: When the two foes combine their strength, what then shall we do?
translations.idiomatic: When the two of them join forces, what will we do then?"

sentences.zh: 」通又請解圍就險以候其變，太宗不許。

translations.literal: Tong again asked to lift the siege and take a strong position to await changes; Taizong would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tu Tong again asked to raise the siege and fall back to defensible ground; Taizong refused.

sentences.zh: 於是留通輔齊王元吉以圍世充，親率步騎三千五百人趣武牢。

translations.literal: Thereupon he left Tong to assist Prince of Qi Yuanji in besieging Shichong and himself led three thousand five hundred foot and horse toward Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: He left Qu Tu Tong with Prince of Qi Yuanji to keep the siege and marched in person with thirty-five hundred foot and horse for Hulao.

sentences.zh: 建德自滎陽西上，築壘於板渚，太宗屯武牢，相持二十餘日。

translations.literal: Jiande came up from west of Xingyang and built ramparts at Banzhu; Taizong encamped at Hulao, and the two sides faced each other for more than twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande advanced from west of Xingyang and fortified Banzhu; Taizong held Hulao. For twenty days the armies watched each other.

sentences.zh: 諜者曰：「建德伺官軍芻盡，候牧馬於河北，因將襲武牢。

translations.literal: Spies reported: "Jiande is watching for our fodder to run out; he plans to wait until we pasture our horses north of the river, then strike Hulao."
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence reported that Jiande meant to wait until Tang fodder gave out, then attack while the horses were grazing north of the river.

sentences.zh: 」太宗知其謀，遂牧馬河北以誘之。

translations.literal: Taizong knew their plan and therefore pastured his horses north of the river to lure them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong saw the trap and deliberately grazed his horses north of the river as bait.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，建德果悉眾而至，陳兵氾水，世充將郭士衡陣於其南，綿互數里，鼓噪，諸將大懼。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day Jiande indeed came with his whole host, drew up his troops along the Fan River, and Shichong's general Guo Shiheng formed to the south, stretching for several li amid clamor; the generals were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Jiande came in full strength, lined the Fan River for miles, and Guo Shiheng, Shichong's general, formed to the south—the din terrified Taizong's officers.

sentences.zh: 太宗將數騎升高丘以望之，謂諸將曰：「賊起山東，未見大敵。

translations.literal: Taizong took a few horsemen up a high mound to look them over and said to the generals: "The rebels rose in Shandong and have never seen a great foe.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong rode to a hill with a handful of men, studied the host, and told his commanders: "These men came out of Shandong and have never met a real army.

sentences.zh: 今度險而囂，是無政令；

translations.literal: Now they cross difficult ground yet are arrogant—that means no discipline;
translations.idiomatic: They have crossed hard country yet strut about—that means no discipline.

sentences.zh: 逼城而陣，有輕我心。

translations.literal: they press the city yet draw up in battle—that shows they hold us light.
translations.idiomatic: They crowd the walls yet offer battle—that means they think little of us.

sentences.zh: 我按兵不出，彼乃氣衰，陣久卒饑，必將自退，追而擊之，無往不克。

translations.literal: If we hold our troops and do not go out, their spirit will fade; when the line stands long the soldiers hunger, and they are sure to withdraw of themselves—pursue and strike, and nowhere will we fail.
translations.idiomatic: Hold still and their spirit will sink; stand in line till noon and they will hunger and pull back. Then pursue—and we cannot fail.

sentences.zh: 吾與公等約，必以午時後破之。

translations.literal: I make this pact with you: we shall break them after the hour wu."
translations.idiomatic: I swear to you—we will break them after noon."

sentences.zh: 」建德列陣，自辰至午，兵士饑倦，皆坐列，又爭飲水，逡巡斂退。

translations.literal: Jiande drew up his formation; from chen to wu the soldiers were hungry and weary, all sitting in their ranks; they also quarreled over drinking water, and after a while drew back.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande formed his line; from morning to noon his men grew hungry and slack, sitting in the ranks, scrambling for water, then edging back.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「可擊矣！

translations.literal: Taizong said: "They can be struck!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong cried: "Now—hit them!"

sentences.zh: 」親率輕騎追而誘之，眾繼至。

translations.literal: " He personally led light cavalry in pursuit to lure them; the masses followed on.
translations.idiomatic: He himself led the light horse forward in a feigned chase; the main body came after.

sentences.zh: 建德回師而陣，未及整列，太宗先登擊之，所向皆靡。

translations.literal: Jiande turned his army and formed; before he could set his ranks in order Taizong was first upon them in the assault; wherever he went, none could stand.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande wheeled to form, but before the ranks settled Taizong was already among them; nothing held against his charge.

sentences.zh: 俄而眾軍合戰，囂塵四起。

translations.literal: Presently the armies joined in battle and dust and clamor rose on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the whole field was locked in battle, dust and shouting everywhere.

sentences.zh: 太宗率史大奈、程咬金、秦叔寶、宇文歆等揮幡而入，直突出其陣後，張我旗幟。

translations.literal: Taizong led Shi Danai, Cheng Yaojin, Qin Shubao, Yu Wenxin, and others, banners waving, straight through to the rear of their formation, and raised our standards.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong with Shi Danai, Cheng Yaojin, Qin Shubao, Yu Wenxin, and others drove their banners through to the enemy rear and planted the Tang colors.

sentences.zh: 賊顧見之，大潰。

translations.literal: When the rebels looked back and saw them, they broke in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy looked behind, saw Tang banners in their rear, and collapsed.

sentences.zh: 追奔三十里，斬首三千餘級，虜其眾五萬，生擒建德於陣。

translations.literal: The pursuit ran thirty li; more than three thousand heads were taken, fifty thousand of their host were captured, and Jiande was seized alive on the field.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit ran thirty li: three thousand heads, fifty thousand prisoners, and Jiande taken alive on the field.

sentences.zh: 太宗數之曰：「我以干戈問罪，本在王世充，得失存亡，不預汝事，何故越境，犯我兵鋒？

translations.literal: Taizong rebuked him, saying: "I took up arms to punish guilt, and that guilt lies with Wang Shichong; gain or loss, survival or ruin, does not concern you—why did you cross the border and strike my army?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong upbraided him: "I marched to punish Wang Shichong. Your quarrel was not mine—why did you cross my border and meet my blades?"

sentences.zh: 」建德股慄而言曰：「今若不來，恐勞遠取。

translations.literal: Jiande trembled in his thighs and said: "Had I not come, I feared you would weary yourself with a distant campaign."
translations.idiomatic: Jiande shook and said: "If I had stayed away, I feared you would wear yourself out marching so far."

sentences.zh: 」高祖聞而大悅，手詔曰；

translations.literal: Gaozu heard and was greatly pleased and wrote with his own hand:
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard, he was overjoyed and wrote in his own hand:

sentences.zh: 「隋氏分崩，崤函隔絕。

translations.literal: "The house of Sui is split asunder; the passes of Xiaoshan and Hangu are cut off.
translations.idiomatic: "The Sui house is broken; Xiaoshan and Hangu stand between us and the east.

sentences.zh: 兩雄合勢，一朝清蕩。

translations.literal: Two mighty foes joined their strength and were swept away in a morning.
translations.idiomatic: Two great enemies joined—and you cleared them in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 兵既克捷，更無死傷。

translations.literal: The army won the victory yet not another man fell.
translations.idiomatic: The battle was won without another man lost.

sentences.zh: 無愧為臣，不憂其父，並汝功也。

translations.literal: A minister without shame, a father without grief—all that is your achievement."
translations.idiomatic: No shame to the minister, no grief to the father—that glory is yours alone."

sentences.zh: 」乃將建德至東都城下。

translations.literal: " He then led Jiande to beneath the walls of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then paraded Jiande before the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 世充懼，率其官屬二千餘人詣軍門請降，山東悉平。

translations.literal: Shichong, in fear, led more than two thousand of his officials to the camp gate to surrender; Shandong was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong, in terror, came with two thousand officials to the camp gate and submitted; Shandong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 太宗入據宮城，令蕭瑀、竇軌等封守府庫，一無所取，令記室房玄齡收隋圖籍。

translations.literal: Taizong entered and held the palace city; he ordered Xiao Yu, Dou Ji, and others to seal the treasuries, taking nothing for themselves, and ordered Recorder Fang Xuanling to gather the Sui maps and registers.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong entered the palace precinct, set Xiao Yu and Dou Ji to seal the vaults without plunder, and had Fang Xuanling collect the Sui archives and maps.

sentences.zh: 於是誅其同惡段達等五十餘人，枉被囚禁者悉釋之，非罪誅戮者祭而誄之。

translations.literal: Thereupon more than fifty of their chief accomplices, including Duan Da, were executed; all who had been wrongly imprisoned were released, and those put to death without cause were mourned and eulogized.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty ringleaders, including Duan Da, were put to death; the innocent were freed, and those wrongly executed were mourned and given posthumous praise.

sentences.zh: 大饗將士，班賜有差。

translations.literal: He held a great feast for the officers and distributed rewards in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted the army and gave rewards by rank.

sentences.zh: 高祖令尚書左僕射裴寂勞於軍中。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Pei Ji to offer congratulations in the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Pei Ji, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, to congratulate the army.

sentences.zh: 六月，凱旋。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he returned in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 太宗親披黃金甲，陣鐵馬一萬騎，甲士三萬人，前後部鼓吹，俘二偽主及隋氏器物輦輅獻於太廟。

translations.literal: Taizong personally donned golden armor, arrayed ten thousand iron-clad horses and thirty thousand armored soldiers, with front and rear bands of martial music, and presented the two bogus rulers and the Sui ritual vessels and imperial carriages at the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wore golden armor, paraded ten thousand armored horses and thirty thousand mail-clad troops with full martial music, and presented the two captive kings and the Sui regalia at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，行飲至禮以享焉。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and performed the ritual of drinking to the army's return to feast him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu rejoiced and held the "drink on return" rite to honor him.

sentences.zh: 高祖以自古舊官不稱殊功，乃別表徽號，用旌勛德。

translations.literal: Gaozu held that from antiquity the old offices could not match extraordinary merit, and therefore set forth separate titles of honor to signal merit and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu judged that ancient titles could not match such merit and created new honors to mark it.

sentences.zh: 十月，加號天策上將、陜東道大行臺，位在王公上。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was given the additional title Heavenly Stratagem General and Chief of the Shaanxi-East Circuit headquarters, ranking above kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he received the added title Heavenly Stratagem General and chief of the Shaanxi-East headquarters, ranking above princes and dukes.

sentences.zh: 增邑二萬戶，通前三萬戶。

translations.literal: His fief was increased by twenty thousand households, making thirty thousand in all with what he had before.
translations.idiomatic: His fief rose by twenty thousand households to thirty thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 賜金輅一乘，袞冕之服，玉璧一雙，黃金六千斤，前後部鼓吹及九部之樂，班劍四十人。

translations.literal: He was granted one golden chariot, robes of the nine symbols, a pair of jade disks, six thousand jin of gold, front and rear martial music and the nine orchestras, and forty ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: He received a golden chariot, full royal regalia, a pair of jade disks, six thousand jin of gold, imperial music, and forty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 於時海內漸平，太宗乃銳意經籍，開文學館以待四方之士。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was gradually pacified, and Taizong turned his keen attention to the classics, opening a Hall of Literary Endeavor to await men of talent from the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: As the realm grew quiet, Taizong turned to scholarship and opened the Hall of Literary Endeavor for scholars from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 行臺司勛郎中杜如晦等十有八人為學士，每更直閣下，降以溫顏，與之討論經義，或夜分而罷。

translations.literal: Du Ruhui of the Circuit Bureau of Merits and eighteen others were made academicians; they took turns on duty below the pavilion, received his warm countenance, and discussed the classics with him—sometimes until deep in the night.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ruhui and eighteen others of the circuit staff became academicians, rotating below the pavilion to debate the classics with him far into the night.

sentences.zh: 未幾，竇建德舊將劉黑闥舉兵反，據洺州。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Heita, a former officer of Dou Jiande, raised troops in revolt and seized Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liu Heita, once Jiande's officer, rebelled and held Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十二月，太宗總戎東討。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Taizong took overall command and marched east to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Taizong took supreme command and marched east against him.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，進軍肥鄉，分兵絕其糧道，相持兩月。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year he advanced on Feixiang, divided his forces to cut the rebel grain route, and faced them for two months.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Wude 5 he moved on Feixiang, detached columns to sever supplies, and held Heita at bay for two months.

sentences.zh: 黑闥窘急求戰，率步騎二萬，南渡洺水，晨壓官軍。

translations.literal: Heita, hard pressed, sought battle; he led twenty thousand foot and horse, crossed the Ming River to the south at dawn, and pressed the imperial army at first light.
translations.idiomatic: Heita, cornered, forced a battle: at dawn he led twenty thousand foot and horse south across the Ming River and struck at daybreak.

sentences.zh: 太宗親率精騎，擊其馬軍，破之，乘勝蹂其步卒，賊大潰，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: Taizong personally led his elite cavalry, struck their horse troops, broke them, pressed the advantage to trample their infantry, and the rebels were utterly routed; more than ten thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong led the elite horse himself, shattered the cavalry, rolled over the foot, and broke Heita completely—more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 先是，太宗遣堰洺水上流使淺，令黑闥得渡。

translations.literal: Earlier Taizong had ordered a dam on the upper Ming to shallow the water so Heita could cross.
translations.idiomatic: Before the fight Taizong had dammed the upper Ming to shallow the river so Heita would cross.

sentences.zh: 及戰，乃令決堰，水大至，深丈餘，賊徒既敗，赴水者皆溺死焉。

translations.literal: When battle came he ordered the dam broken; the water rose greatly, more than a zhang deep, and when the rebels were already beaten, those who ran into the water all drowned.
translations.idiomatic: At the clash he had the dam opened; the flood rose more than ten feet, and the broken army drowned in the Ming by the thousands.

sentences.zh: 黑闥與二百餘騎北走突厥，悉虜其眾，河北平。

translations.literal: Heida fled north to the Turks with more than two hundred horsemen; all his followers were taken captive; Hebei was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Heida fled north to the Turks with some two hundred riders; his remaining forces were captured, and Hebei was pacified.

sentences.zh: 時徐圓朗阻兵徐、兗，太宗回師討平之，於是河、濟、江、淮諸郡邑皆平。

translations.literal: At that time Xu Yuanlang held out with arms in Xu and Yan, and the Prince of Qin turned his army back to attack and pacify him; thereafter all prefectures and counties along the Yellow, Ji, Yangzi, and Huai were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanlang still held Xu and Yan with armed force; Taizong swung his army south, subdued him, and brought the Yellow, Ji, Yangzi, and Huai regions under control.

sentences.zh: 十月，加左右十二衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was additionally made Grand General of the Left and Right Twelve Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was made Grand General of the Left and Right Twelve Guards.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，突厥頡利、突利二可汗自原州入寇，侵擾關中。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year, the Turk qaghans Jieli and Tuli entered from Yuanzhou to raid and harass Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Turk qaghans Jieli and Tuli invaded from Yuanzhou and raided Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 有說高祖云：「只為府藏子女在京師，故突厥來，若燒卻長安而不都，則胡寇自止。

translations.literal: Someone told Gaozu: "It is only because the treasury and women and children are in the capital that the Turks come. If Chang'an were burned and the capital abandoned, the barbarian raiders would stop of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: An adviser told Gaozu: "The Turks come only because the treasury and the court's families are in Chang'an. Burn the city, move the capital, and the raids will end on their own.

sentences.zh: 」高祖乃遣中書侍郎宇文士及行山南可居之地，即欲移都。

translations.literal: " Gaozu thereupon sent Vice Director of the Secretariat Yuwen Shiji to survey habitable lands south of the mountains, intending at once to move the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu sent Secretariat Vice Director Yuwen Shiji to scout habitable country south of the Qinling range and prepared to move the capital at once.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀等皆以為非，然終不敢犯顏正諫。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu and others all considered it wrong, but in the end none dared remonstrate to his face.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu and the others all opposed the plan, yet none dared speak bluntly to the Emperor's face.

sentences.zh: 太宗獨曰：「霍去病，漢廷之將帥耳，猶且志滅匈奴。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin alone said: "Huo Qubing was only a commander of the Han court, yet he aspired to destroy the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong alone replied: "Huo Qubing was merely a Han general, yet he set his heart on destroying the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 臣忝備籓維，尚使胡塵不息，遂令陛下議欲遷都，此臣之責也。

translations.literal: I, unworthy though I am placed in the ranks of the princes, have still allowed the dust of the barbarians to rise unceasingly, until Your Majesty debates moving the capital — this is my fault.
translations.idiomatic: I hold a prince's commission, yet barbarian dust still clouds the frontier and Your Majesty must even consider abandoning Chang'an — the fault is mine.

sentences.zh: 幸乞聽臣一申微效，取彼頡利。

translations.literal: I beg you to allow me to exert what little strength I have once more and take that Jieli.
translations.idiomatic: Grant me one more chance to prove myself and I will bring you Jieli's head.

sentences.zh: 若一兩年間不系其頸，徐建移都之策，臣當不敢復言」。

translations.literal: If within a year or two I do not have him by the neck, then by slow steps consider a plan to move the capital — I shall not dare speak again."
translations.idiomatic: If I fail to collar him within a year or two, then discuss relocation at leisure — and I will never raise the matter again."

sentences.zh: 高祖怒，仍遣太宗將三十餘騎行刬。

translations.literal: Gaozu was angry, but still sent the Prince of Qin with thirty-odd riders on a reconnaissance raid.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was furious, yet still sent Taizong with a few dozen horsemen on a probing strike.

sentences.zh: 還日，固奏必不可移都，高祖遂止。

translations.literal: On the day he returned, he firmly memorialized that the capital must under no circumstances be moved, and Gaozu thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned he memorialized again that the capital must not be moved, and Gaozu abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 八年，加中書令。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was additionally made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武德九年九年，皇太子建成、齊王元吉謀害太宗。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Wude, Crown Prince Jiancheng and Prince of Qi Yuanji plotted to harm the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Wude, Crown Prince Li Jiancheng and Prince of Qi Li Yuanji plotted to kill Taizong.

sentences.zh: 六月四日，太宗率長孫無忌、尉遲敬德、房玄齡、杜如晦、宇文士及、高士廉、侯君集、程知節、秦叔寶、段志玄、屈突通、張士貴等於玄武門誅之。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the sixth month the Prince of Qin led Zhangsun Wuji, Yuchi Jingde, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Yuwen Shiji, Gao Shilian, Hou Junji, Cheng Zhijie, Qin Shubao, Duan Zhixuan, Qu Tu Tong, Zhang Shigui, and others at the Xuanwu Gate to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the sixth month Taizong led Zhangsun Wuji, Yuchi Jingde, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Yuwen Shiji, Gao Shilian, Hou Junji, Cheng Zhijie, Qin Shubao, Duan Zhixuan, Qu Tu Tong, Zhang Shigui, and others to ambush and kill them at the Xuanwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 甲子，立為皇太子，庶政皆斷決。

translations.literal: On jiazi he was installed as crown prince, and all routine government was decided by him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he was named crown prince and took charge of daily administration.

sentences.zh: 太宗乃縱禁苑所養鷹犬，並停諸方所進珍異，政尚簡肅，天下大悅。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin then released the hawks and hounds raised in the forbidden park, halted all rare curios submitted from the regions, inclined government toward simplicity and severity, and all under Heaven rejoiced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He freed the hunting birds and dogs kept in the imperial park, stopped exotic tribute from the provinces, governed with austere simplicity, and the realm rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 又令百官各上封事，備陳安人理國之要。

translations.literal: He also ordered the hundred officials each to submit sealed memorials setting forth fully the essentials of settling the people and governing the state.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered every official to submit sealed memorials on how to settle the people and govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 己巳，令曰：「依禮，二名不偏諱。

translations.literal: On jisi an edict said: "According to ritual, taboo on double personal names is not applied to a single character.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi an edict declared: "By classical rite, a two-character personal name is not tabooed when only one character appears.

sentences.zh: 近代已來，兩字兼避，廢闕已多，率意而行，有違經典。

translations.literal: In recent times both characters have been avoided together, and many words have been abandoned — acting as inclination leads violates the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Lately both characters have been avoided everywhere, countless words have been lost, and custom has departed from the canon.

sentences.zh: 其官號、人名、公私文籍，有『世民』兩字不連續者，並不須諱。

translations.literal: In official titles, personal names, and public and private documents, wherever the two characters Shimin are not consecutive, avoidance is not required.
translations.idiomatic: In titles, names, and public or private writing, wherever the characters for Shimin do not stand together, no avoidance is required.

sentences.zh: 」罷幽州大都督府。

translations.literal: " The Youzhou Metropolitan Protectorate was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Youzhou metropolitan protectorate was abolished.

sentences.zh: 辛未，廢陜東道大行臺，置洛州都督府，廢益州道行臺，置益州大都督府。

translations.literal: On xinwei the Shaanxi East Circuit Grand Secretariat was abolished and a Luozhou Protectorate established; the Yizhou Circuit mobile secretariat was abolished and a Yizhou Metropolitan Protectorate established.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the Shaanxi east circuit headquarters was dissolved and a Luozhou protectorate set up; the Yizhou circuit headquarters was dissolved and a Yizhou metropolitan protectorate set up.

sentences.zh: 壬午，幽州大都督廬江王瑗謀逆，廢為庶人。

translations.literal: On renwu Prince Yuan of Lujiang, Metropolitan Protector of Youzhou, plotted rebellion and was degraded to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Li Yuan of Lujiang, metropolitan protector of Youzhou, plotted rebellion and was reduced to commoner rank.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，罷天策府。

translations.literal: On yiyou the Celestial-Strategy Office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou the Celestial-Strategy headquarters was abolished.

sentences.zh: 七月壬辰，太子左庶子高士廉為侍中，右庶子房玄齡為中書令，尚書右僕射蕭瑀為尚書左僕射，吏部尚書楊恭仁為雍州牧，太子左庶子長孫無忌為吏部尚書，右庶子杜如晦為兵部尚書，太子詹事宇文士及為中書令，封德彞為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On renchen of the seventh month Senior Advisor to the Crown Prince Gao Shilian became Palace Attendant; Junior Advisor Fang Xuanling became Director of the Secretariat; Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xiao Yu became Left Vice Director; Minister of Personnel Yang Gongren became Prefect of Yongzhou; Senior Advisor Zhangsun Wuji became Minister of Personnel; Junior Advisor Du Ruhui became Minister of War; Grand Steward of the Heir Apparent Yuwen Shiji became Director of the Secretariat; Feng Deyi became Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen of the seventh month Gao Shilian moved from senior adviser to the heir to Palace Attendant; Fang Xuanling from junior adviser to Secretariat Director; Xiao Yu from right to left vice director of the Masters of Writing; Yang Gongren from Minister of Personnel to Yongzhou prefect; Zhangsun Wuji to Minister of Personnel; Du Ruhui to Minister of War; Yuwen Shiji to Secretariat Director; and Feng Deyi to right vice director.

sentences.zh: 八月癸亥，高祖傳位於皇太子，太宗即位於東宮顯德殿。

translations.literal: On guihai of the eighth month Gaozu transmitted the throne to the crown prince; the Prince of Qin took the throne at the Xiande Hall of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai of the eighth month Gaozu abdicated in favor of the crown prince; Taizong ascended the throne in the Xiande Hall of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 遣司空、魏國公裴寂柴告於南郊。

translations.literal: He sent Minister of Works, Duke of Wei Pei Ji with a firewood offering to report at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Pei Ji, Duke of Wei and Minister of Works, to offer firewood at the southern altar and announce the succession to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 武德元年以來責情流配者並放還。

translations.literal: All persons exiled by sentence according to aggravated circumstances since the first year of Wude were released and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone exiled on aggravated charges since the first year of Wude was pardoned and sent home.

sentences.zh: 文武官五品已上先無爵者賜爵一級，六品已下加勛一轉。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above who previously had no noble rank were granted one step of rank; those of the sixth rank and below received one grade of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of fifth rank and above without titles received a noble rank; those of sixth rank and below received an extra grade of merit.

sentences.zh: 天下給復一年。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm taxes were remitted for one year.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were waived empire-wide for one year.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，放掖庭宮女三千餘人。

translations.literal: On guiyou more than three thousand palace women of the Inner Quarters were released.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou more than three thousand women of the inner palace were freed.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，突厥頡利、突利寇涇州。

translations.literal: On jiaxu the Turk qaghans Jieli and Tuli raided Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the Turk qaghans Jieli and Tuli attacked Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，突厥進寇武功，京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: On yihai the Turks pressed on to raid Wugong; the capital was placed under alert.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the Turks advanced on Wugong and Chang'an was placed under martial alert.

sentences.zh: 丙子，立妃長孫氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On bingzi Consort Changsun was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Lady Changsun was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 己卯，突厥寇高陵。

translations.literal: On jimao the Turks raided Gaoling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the Turks struck Gaoling.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，行軍總管尉遲敬德與突厥戰於涇陽，大破之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: On xinsi Campaign Commander Yuchi Jingde fought the Turks at Jingyang, routed them greatly, and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Yuchi Jingde, campaign commander, met the Turks at Jingyang, crushed them, and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 癸未，突厥頡利至於渭水便橋之北，遣其酋帥執失思力入朝為覘，自張形勢，太宗命囚之。

translations.literal: On guiwei Jieli reached the north bank of the Bian Bridge on the Wei River, sent his chieftain Zhishi Sili to court on reconnaissance and displayed his forces openly; the Emperor ordered him imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Jieli camped north of the Bian Bridge on the Wei; he sent the chieftain Zhishi Sili to court as a spy and paraded his strength — the Emperor had him seized.

sentences.zh: 親出玄武門，馳六騎幸渭水上，與頡利隔津而語，責以負約。

translations.literal: In person he went out the Xuanwu Gate, galloped with six riders to the Wei River, spoke with Jieli across the ford, and reproached him for breaking faith.
translations.idiomatic: He rode out the Xuanwu Gate himself with six horsemen to the Wei, hailed Jieli across the water, and rebuked him for breaking treaty.

sentences.zh: 俄而眾軍繼至，頡利見軍容既盛，又知思力就拘，由是大懼，遂請和，詔許焉。

translations.literal: Before long the main armies arrived; Jieli saw the troops already strong and knew Zhishi Sili had been detained; he was greatly afraid and sued for peace; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the main forces came up; seeing their array and learning his envoy was held, Jieli was terrified and sued for peace, which the Emperor granted.

sentences.zh: 即日還宮。

translations.literal: That same day he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: That day he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，又幸便橋，與頡利刑白馬設盟，突厥引退。

translations.literal: On yiyou he again visited Bian Bridge; with Jieli he cut a white horse and established alliance; the Turks withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou he returned to the Bian Bridge, slew a white horse with Jieli to seal a pact, and the Turks withdrew.

sentences.zh: 九月丙戌，頡利獻馬三千匹、羊萬口，帝不受，令頡利歸所掠中國戶口。

translations.literal: On bingxu Jieli presented three thousand horses and ten thousand sheep; the Emperor did not accept them and ordered Jieli to return the Chinese households he had seized.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Jieli offered three thousand horses and ten thousand sheep; the Emperor refused the gift and demanded the return of captured Chinese subjects.

sentences.zh: 丁未，引諸衛騎兵統將等習射於顯德殿庭，謂將軍已下曰：「自古突厥與中國更有盛衰。

translations.literal: On dingwei he summoned the cavalry commanders of the guards to practice archery in the courtyard of the Xiande Hall and said to the generals and below: "From antiquity the Turks and China have each known rise and decline.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he gathered the guard cavalry officers for archery drill in the Xiande Hall courtyard and told the commanders: "Turks and China have waxed and waned since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 若軒轅善用五兵，即能北逐獯鬻；

translations.literal: When the Yellow Emperor well employed the five weapons, he was able to drive the Xianyun north;
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow Emperor mastered the five arms, he drove the Xianyun north;

sentences.zh: 周宣驅馳方、召，亦能制勝太原。

translations.literal: when King Xuan of Zhou deployed the Fang and Shao, he too could prevail over Taiyuan.
