translations.idiomatic: when King Xuan of Zhou sent Fang and Shao, he too mastered the north.

sentences.zh: 至漢、晉之君，逮於隋代，不使兵士素習干戈，突厥來侵，莫能抗禦，致遺中國生民塗炭於寇手。

translations.literal: Down through the Han and Jin rulers to the Sui, they did not keep soldiers trained in arms; when the Turks came they could not resist, and the living people of China were smeared by the raiders' hands.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Jin through Sui, rulers let arms training lapse; when Turks struck, China could not defend herself, and her people paid in blood.

sentences.zh: 我今不使汝等穿池築苑，造諸淫費，農民恣令逸樂，兵士唯習弓馬，庶使汝鬥戰，亦望汝前無橫敵。

translations.literal: I now will not have you dig pools and build parks or make all manner of wasteful expense; farmers I leave to their ease, and soldiers I have practice only bow and horse — I intend that you fight in battle, and I hope that before you no enemy stands athwart your path.
translations.idiomatic: I will not have you dig parks or squander treasure; farmers may rest while soldiers train only with bow and horse — I mean you to fight, and I expect no foe to stand before you.

sentences.zh: 」於是每日引數百人於殿前教射，帝親自臨試，射中者隨賞弓刀、布帛。

translations.literal: " Thereafter each day he led several hundred men before the hall to teach archery; the Emperor personally tested them, and those who hit the mark were rewarded with bows, blades, cloth, and silk.
translations.idiomatic: " Each day thereafter he drilled several hundred men in archery before the hall, tested them himself, and rewarded hits with bows, blades, cloth, and silk.

sentences.zh: 朝臣多有諫者，曰：「先王制法，有以兵刃至御所者刑之，所以防萌杜漸，備不虞也。

translations.literal: Many court ministers remonstrated, saying: "The former kings made law: whoever brought weapons to the imperial precinct was punished — thus to nip evil in the bud and guard against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers objected: "Ancient law punished anyone who brought arms to the throne room — a guard against sudden harm.

sentences.zh: 今引裨卒之人，彎弧縱矢於軒陛之側，陛下親在其間，正恐禍出非意，非所以為社稷計也。

translations.literal: Now you lead common soldiers to draw bows beside the palace steps while Your Majesty stands among them — we fear harm may come from an unexpected quarter; this is not planning for the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Now common soldiers bend bows on the palace steps while Your Majesty stands among them — disaster may come from nowhere; this does not secure the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 」上不納。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 自是後，士卒皆為精銳。

translations.literal: From this time forward the soldiers all became elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the army became a corps of veterans.

sentences.zh: 壬子，詔私家不得輒立妖神，妄設淫祀，非禮祠禱，一皆禁絕。

translations.literal: On renzi an edict said: "Private persons must not presumptuously set up demonic spirits or establish improper sacrifices; all prayers outside ritual are utterly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi an edict forbade private cults to rogue spirits, illicit shrines, and all prayer outside orthodox rite.

sentences.zh: 其龜易五兆之外，諸雜占卜，亦皆停斷。

translations.literal: Beyond the tortoise and the Changes and the Five Omens, all miscellaneous divination was also stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Divination beyond the tortoise, the Changes, and the Five Omens was likewise banned.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌封齊國公，房玄齡邢國公，尉遲敬德吳國公，杜如晦蔡國公，侯君集潞國公。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji was enfeoffed Duke of Qi, Fang Xuanling Duke of Xing, Yuchi Jingde Duke of Wu, Du Ruhui Duke of Cai, and Hou Junji Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji was created Duke of Qi, Fang Xuanling Duke of Xing, Yuchi Jingde Duke of Wu, Du Ruhui Duke of Cai, and Hou Junji Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙辰朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the tenth winter month, on bingchen the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, the first day of the tenth winter month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，立中山王承乾為皇太子。

translations.literal: On guihai Prince Chengqian of Zhongshan was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Li Chengqian, Prince of Zhongshan, was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，裴寂食實封一千五百戶，長孫無忌、王君廓、尉遲敬德、房玄齡、杜如晦一千三百戶，長孫順德、柴紹、羅藝、趙郡王孝恭一千二百戶，侯君集、張公謹、劉師立一千戶，李世勣、劉弘基九百戶，高士廉、宇文士及、秦叔寶、程知節七百戶，安興貴、安修仁、唐儉、竇軌、屈突通、蕭瑀、封德彞、劉義節六百戶，錢九隴、樊世興、公孫武達、李孟常、段志玄、龐卿惲、張亮、李藥師、杜淹、元仲文四百戶，張長遜、張平高、李安遠、李子和、秦行師、馬三寶三百戶。

translations.literal: On guiyou Pei Ji received a permanent fief of one thousand five hundred households; Zhangsun Wuji, Wang Junguo, Yuchi Jingde, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui one thousand three hundred each; Zhangsun Shunde, Chai Shao, Luo Yi, and Prince of Zhao Commandery Xiaogong one thousand two hundred each; Hou Junji, Zhang Gongjin, and Liu Shili one thousand each; Li Shiji and Liu Hongji nine hundred each; Gao Shilian, Yuwen Shiji, Qin Shubao, and Cheng Zhijie seven hundred each; An Xinggui, An Xiuren, Tang Jian, Dou Gui, Qu Tu Tong, Xiao Yu, Feng Deyi, and Liu Yijie six hundred each; Qian Jiulong, Fan Shixing, Gongsun Wuda, Li Mengchang, Duan Zhixuan, Pang Qingyun, Zhang Liang, Li Yaoshi, Du Yan, and Yuan Zhongwen four hundred each; Zhang Changsun, Zhang Pinggao, Li Anyuan, Li Zihe, Qin Xingshi, and Ma Sanbao three hundred each.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou permanent fiefs were granted: Pei Ji fifteen hundred households; Zhangsun Wuji, Wang Junguo, Yuchi Jingde, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui thirteen hundred each; Zhangsun Shunde, Chai Shao, Luo Yi, and Prince Xiaogong of Zhao twelve hundred each; Hou Junji, Zhang Gongjin, and Liu Shili one thousand each; Li Shiji and Liu Hongji nine hundred each; Gao Shilian, Yuwen Shiji, Qin Shubao, and Cheng Zhijie seven hundred each; An Xinggui, An Xiuren, Tang Jian, Dou Gui, Qu Tu Tong, Xiao Yu, Feng Deyi, and Liu Yijie six hundred each; Qian Jiulong, Fan Shixing, Gongsun Wuda, Li Mengchang, Duan Zhixuan, Pang Qingyun, Zhang Liang, Li Yaoshi, Du Yan, and Yuan Zhongwen four hundred each; and Zhang Changsun, Zhang Pinggao, Li Anyuan, Li Zihe, Qin Xingshi, and Ma Sanbao three hundred each.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚寅，降宗室封郡王者並為縣公。

translations.literal: On gengyin of the eleventh month princes of the imperial clan enfeoffed as commandery kings were all reduced to county marquises.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin of the eleventh month imperial princes holding commandery-king titles were demoted to county marquises.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸酉，親錄囚徒。

translations.literal: On guiyou of the twelfth month he personally reviewed prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou of the twelfth month he reviewed prisoners in person.

sentences.zh: 是歲，新羅、龜茲、突厥、高麗、百濟、黨項並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That year Silla, Kucha, the Turks, Goguryeo, Baekje, and the Tangut all sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Silla, Kucha, the Turks, Goguryeo, Baekje, and the Tangut presented tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年貞觀元年春正月乙酉，改元。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, in the spring of the first month, on yiyou, the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan, on yiyou of the first spring month, the reign title was changed.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，燕郡王李藝據涇州反，尋為左右所斬，傳首京師。

translations.literal: On xinchou Prince Yi of Yan Commandery seized Jing Prefecture in rebellion; before long he was beheaded by his own attendants and his head sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Li Yi, Prince of Yan Commandery, rebelled at Jingzhou; his own guards soon killed him and sent his head to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以僕射竇軌為益州大都督。

translations.literal: On gengwu the Vice Director Pei Gui was made Metropolitan Protector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Pei Gui, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was appointed metropolitan protector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 三月癸巳，皇后親蠶。

translations.literal: On guisi of the third month the empress personally performed the sericulture rite.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi of the third month the empress led the spring silkworm ceremony.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射、宋國公蕭瑀為太子少師。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Song Xiao Yu became Junior Tutor to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu, Duke of Song and left vice director of the Masters of Writing, became junior tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 丙午，詔：「齊故尚書僕射崔季舒、給事黃門侍郎郭遵、尚書右丞封孝琰等，昔仕鄴中，名位通顯，志存忠讜，抗表極言，無救社稷之亡，遂見龍逢之酷。

translations.literal: On bingwu an edict said: "Cui Jishu, former Vice Director of the Masters of Writing of Qi; Guo Zun, Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate; and Feng Xiaoyan, Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing — in former days they served Ye, held eminent name and office, cherished loyal remonstrance in their hearts, and submitted forthright memorials; they could not save their state from ruin and met the cruel fate of Long Feng.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu an edict recalled Cui Jishu, Guo Zun, and Feng Xiaoyan of Northern Qi — men of high office who spoke truth to power at Ye, could not save their state, and died like Long Feng.

sentences.zh: 其季舒子剛、遵子雲、孝琰子君遵，並以門遭時譴，淫刑濫及。

translations.literal: Their sons Gang, Yun, and Junzun, because their houses suffered the calamity of the times, were struck by excessive punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Their sons Cui Gang, Guo Yun, and Feng Junzun had suffered exile and harsh punishment with their families.

sentences.zh: 宜從褒獎，特異常倫，可免內侍，量才別敘。

translations.literal: They should receive special reward beyond the usual rule; they may be released from palace service and appointed according to their talents.
translations.idiomatic: They were to be honored beyond ordinary measure, released from menial palace service, and given posts suited to their ability.
Thus ran the edict.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸巳，涼州都督、長樂王幼良有罪伏誅。

translations.literal: In the fourth summer month, on guisi, Liang Prefecture Protector, Prince of Changle Youliang was guilty and executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth summer month, on guisi, Li Youliang, Prince of Changle and protector of Liangzhou, was executed for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 六月辛巳，尚書右僕射、密國公封德彞薨。

translations.literal: On xinsi Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Mi Feng Deyi died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Feng Deyi, Duke of Mi and right vice director of the Masters of Writing, died.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，太子少保宋國公蕭瑀為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On renchen Junior Tutor to the crown prince, Duke of Song Xiao Yu became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Xiao Yu, Duke of Song and junior tutor to the crown prince, became left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 是夏，山東諸州大旱，令所在賑恤，無出今年租賦。

translations.literal: That summer great drought struck the Shandong prefectures; an order was issued to relieve distress wherever it occurred and not to collect that year's land tax.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Shandong suffered severe drought; the court ordered local relief and waived the year's land tax.

sentences.zh: 秋七月壬子，吏部尚書、齊國公長孫無忌為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on renzi, Minister of Personnel, Duke of Qi Zhangsun Wuji became Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on renzi, Zhangsun Wuji, Duke of Qi and Minister of Personnel, became right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 八月戊戌，貶侍中、義興郡公高士廉為安州大都督。

translations.literal: On wuxu Palace Attendant, Duke of Yixing Gao Shilian was demoted to Metropolitan Protector of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Gao Shilian, Duke of Yixing and Palace Attendant, was demoted to metropolitan protector of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書裴矩卒。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Pei Ju died.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju, Minister of Revenue, died.

sentences.zh: 是月，關東及河南、隴右沿邊諸州霜害秋稼。

translations.literal: That month frost damaged the autumn crops in the eastern passes and along Henan and the Longyou frontier prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: That month frost ruined the autumn harvest in the east, Henan, and the Longyou frontier.

sentences.zh: 九月辛酉，命中書侍郎溫彥博、尚書右丞魏徵等分往諸州賑恤。

translations.literal: On xinyou he ordered Secretariat Vice Director Wen Yanbo, Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Wei Zheng, and others to go to the various prefectures to relieve distress.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou he sent Secretariat Vice Director Wen Yanbo, Right Assistant Director Wei Zheng, and others to the provinces on famine relief.

sentences.zh: 中書令、郢國公宇文士及為殿中監。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat, Duke of Ying Yuwen Shiji became Director of the Palace Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shiji, Duke of Ying and Secretariat Director, became director of the palace bureau.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫、檢校吏部尚書、參預朝政、安吉郡公杜淹署位。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief, Acting Minister of Personnel, Participant in Government Affairs, Duke of Anji Du Yan left his post.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan, Duke of Anji, censor-in-chief and acting Minister of Personnel, left office.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬午，上謂侍臣曰：「神仙事本虛妄，空有其名。

translations.literal: On renwu the Emperor said to his attending ministers: "The matter of immortals is fundamentally empty and false — it has only a name.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu the Emperor told his ministers: "Immortality is a lie — nothing but a name.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇非分愛好，遂為方士所詐，乃遣童男女數千人隨徐福入海求仙藥，方士避秦苛虐，因留不歸。

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin had an improper fondness for it and was deceived by masters of the methods; he sent several thousand boys and girls to follow Xu Fu across the sea in search of the elixir of immortality; the masters, fleeing Qin's harsh cruelty, remained abroad and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang's obsession led fangshi to trick him; he sent thousands of youths with Xu Fu to seek elixirs across the sea, and the adepts, fleeing Qin's cruelty, never came back.

sentences.zh: 始皇猶海側踟躕以待之，還至沙丘而死。

translations.literal: The First Emperor still lingered on the seashore waiting for them and died at Shaqiu on his return.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor waited on the shore until he died at Shaqiu on the homeward march.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝為求仙，乃將女嫁道術人，事既無驗，便行誅戮。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han sought immortality and even gave his daughter in marriage to a man of the Way; when nothing came of it, he had the man executed.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi sought immortality, married a princess to a Daoist adept, and when the rites failed, executed him.

sentences.zh: 據此二事，神仙不煩妄求也。

translations.literal: Judging from these two affairs, immortals need not be sought in vain."
translations.idiomatic: These two tales should warn anyone against chasing immortals."

sentences.zh: 」尚書左僕射、宋國公蕭瑀坐事免。

translations.literal: " Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Song Xiao Yu was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu, Duke of Song and left vice director of the Masters of Writing, was dismissed for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 戊申，利州都督義安王孝常、右武衛將軍劉德裕等謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: On wushen Liang Prefecture Protector Prince Xiaochang of Yi'an, Right Martial Guard General Liu Deyu, and others plotted rebellion and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Li Xiaochang, Prince of Yi'an and protector of Lizhou, Right Martial Guard General Liu Deyu, and others plotted rebellion and were executed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，關中饑，至有鬻男女者。

translations.literal: That year famine struck Guanzhong, until there were those who sold sons and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: That year Guanzhong starved so badly that parents sold their children.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年二年春正月辛丑，尚書右僕射、齊國公長孫無忌為開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan, in the spring of the first month, on xinchou, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Qi Zhangsun Wuji became Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon of the same precedence as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenguan, on xinchou of the first spring month, Zhangsun Wuji, Duke of Qi and right vice director, was made Grand Master of Honor with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 徙封漢王屬為恪王，衛王泰為越王，楚王祐為燕王。

translations.literal: Prince of Han Shu was moved to Prince of Ke; Prince of Wei Tai to Prince of Yue; Prince of Chu You to Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shu of Han was retitled Prince of Ke; Prince Tai of Wei became Prince of Yue; Prince You of Chu became Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 復置六侍郎，副六尚書事，並置左右司郎中各一人。

translations.literal: The six vice directors were restored to assist the six ministers, and one Left and one Right Bureau Director were also established.
translations.idiomatic: Six vice directors were restored under the six ministries, each ministry gaining left and right bureau directors.

sentences.zh: 前安州大都督、趙王元景為雍州牧，蜀王恪為益州大都督，越王泰為揚州大都督。

translations.literal: Former Metropolitan Protector of Anzhou, Prince Yuanjing of Zhao became Prefect of Yongzhou; Prince Ke of Shu became Metropolitan Protector of Yizhou; Prince Tai of Yue became Metropolitan Protector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanjing, former metropolitan protector of Anzhou and Prince of Zhao, became Yongzhou prefect; Li Ke, Prince of Shu, metropolitan protector of Yizhou; and Li Tai, Prince of Yue, metropolitan protector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二月丙戌，靺鞨內屬。

translations.literal: On bingxu the Mohe submitted and came within the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the Mohe tribes submitted to Tang rule.

sentences.zh: 三月戊申朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On wushen, the first day of the third month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, the first day of the third month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，遣御史大夫杜淹巡關內諸州。

translations.literal: On dingmao he sent Censor-in-Chief Du Yan to tour the Guanzhong prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he dispatched Censor-in-Chief Du Yan to inspect the Guanzhong prefectures.

sentences.zh: 出御府金寶，贖男女自賣者還其父母。

translations.literal: He released imperial gold and treasure to redeem boys and girls who had sold themselves and return them to their parents.
translations.idiomatic: He drew on the imperial treasury to buy back children sold into bondage and restore them to their parents.

sentences.zh: 庚午，大赦天下。

translations.literal: On gengwu there was a general amnesty throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu he proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 夏四月己卯，詔骸骨暴露者，令所在埋瘞。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on jimao, an edict ordered that wherever exposed bones lay, local authorities were to bury them.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao in the fourth summer month he decreed that exposed remains everywhere were to be interred.

sentences.zh: 丙申，契丹內屬。

translations.literal: On bingshen the Khitan submitted to inner allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the Khitan came within the fold.

sentences.zh: 初詔天下州縣並置義倉。

translations.literal: For the first time an edict ordered charity granaries established in every prefecture and county under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He first commanded charity granaries in every prefecture and county throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 夏州賊帥梁師都為其從父弟洛仁所殺，以城降。

translations.literal: Liang Shidu, bandit chief of Xiazhou, was killed by his younger cousin Luoren, who surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shidu, rebel leader at Xiazhou, was slain by his cousin Luoren, who then surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 五月，大雨雹。

translations.literal: In the fifth month there was heavy hail.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month hail fell in abundance.

sentences.zh: 六月庚寅，皇子治生，宴五品以上，賜帛有差，仍賜天下是日生者粟。

translations.literal: On the sixth month, gengyin, the prince Zhi was born; officials of the fifth rank and above were feasted, silk was bestowed in graded amounts, and grain was granted to every person born on that day throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin of the sixth month Prince Zhi was born. The emperor entertained officials of the fifth rank and above and distributed graded gifts of silk; every child born in the realm on that day received a grant of grain.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，上謂侍臣曰：「君雖不君，臣不可以不臣。

translations.literal: On xinmao the emperor said to his attendant ministers: "Though a lord may fail as lord, a minister may not fail as minister."
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao he told his ministers: "A ruler may fail as ruler, but a minister must not fail as minister."

sentences.zh: 裴虔通，煬帝舊左右也，而親為亂首。

translations.literal: Pei Qiantong had been an intimate attendant of Emperor Yang, yet he himself became the ringleader of the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Qiantong had been one of Yang's closest retainers—yet he led the coup himself.

sentences.zh: 朕方崇獎敬義，豈可猶使宰民訓俗。

translations.literal: I am now promoting reverence and righteousness—how can I still let him hold office over the people and instruct custom?
translations.idiomatic: I mean to exalt loyalty and duty; how could I still let such a man govern the people and set the moral tone?

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：

translations.literal: " An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon issued an edict:

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊申，詔：「萊州刺史牛方裕、絳州刺史薛世良、廣州都督府長史唐奉義、隋武牙郎將高元禮，並於隋代俱蒙任用，乃協契宇文化及，構成弒逆。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on wushen, an edict: "Prefect of Laizhou Niu Fangyu, Prefect of Jiangzhou Xue Shiliang, Chief Administrator of the Guangzhou Protectorate Tang Fengyi, and Sui military adjutant of Wuya Gao Yuanli—all had received office under the Sui, yet they entered into compact with Yu Wen Huaji and participated in regicide."
translations.idiomatic: On wushen of the seventh autumn month he proclaimed: "Niu Fangyu, prefect of Laizhou; Xue Shiliang, prefect of Jiangzhou; Tang Fengyi, chief administrator of Guangzhou; and Gao Yuanli, a Sui adjutant of Wuya—all had held office under the Sui, yet they conspired with Yu Wen Huaji in the murder of the emperor."

sentences.zh: 宜依裴虔通，除名配流嶺表。

translations.literal: They should follow Pei Qiantong's precedent—stripped of names and banished to Lingbiao.
translations.idiomatic: Let them be treated like Pei Qiantong: name struck from the rolls and exiled beyond the southern ranges.

sentences.zh: 」太宗謂侍臣曰：「天下愚人，好犯憲章，凡赦宥之恩，唯及不軌之輩。

translations.literal: " Taizong said to his attendant ministers: "The foolish under heaven love to violate the laws; as for pardons and grace, they should reach only those who have not gone against the norm."
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong told his ministers: "The ignorant everywhere delight in breaking the law. An act of grace should extend only to those who have not crossed the line of rebellion."

sentences.zh: 古語曰：『小人之幸，君子之不幸。

translations.literal: An ancient saying runs: "The good fortune of petty men is the misfortune of gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: As the ancients said: "When petty men prosper, gentlemen suffer."

sentences.zh: 』『一歲再赦，好人喑啞。

translations.literal: "When amnesties come twice in one year, good people are struck dumb."
translations.idiomatic: "Two amnesties in a single year leave honest men speechless."

sentences.zh: 』凡養稂莠者傷禾稼，惠奸宄者賊良人。

translations.literal: To nurture darnel harms the grain; to favor traitors is to rob honest people.
translations.idiomatic: Nurturing weeds ruins the crop; coddling criminals harms the upright.

sentences.zh: 昔文王作罰，刑茲無赦。

translations.literal: In antiquity King Wen established punishments with the rule that in such cases there was no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago King Wen laid down punishments with the rule that certain crimes admitted no pardon.

sentences.zh: 又蜀先主嘗謂諸葛亮曰：『吾周旋陳元方、鄭康成間，每見啟告理亂之道備矣，曾不語赦也。

translations.literal: Again, the Former Lord of Shu once said to Zhuge Liang: "In my time moving among Chen Yuanfang and Zheng Kangcheng, whenever counsel on ordering or chaos was given it was thorough—but never did they speak of amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: The Former Lord of Shu once told Zhuge Liang: "Among Chen Yuanfang and Zheng Kangcheng I heard every argument for order and against chaos—yet never once did they speak of amnesty."

sentences.zh: 』夫小人者，大人之賊，故朕有天下已來，不甚放赦。

translations.literal: Petty men are the enemies of great men; therefore since I have held the realm I have not widely granted amnesties.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men are the enemies of the worthy; that is why, since I took the throne, I have seldom proclaimed amnesty.

sentences.zh: 今四海安靜，禮義興行，非常之恩，施不可數，將恐愚人常冀僥幸，唯欲犯法，不能改過。

translations.literal: Now the four seas are quiet and ritual and righteousness flourish; extraordinary grace cannot be dispensed repeatedly, lest the foolish always hope for luck, seek only to break the law, and fail to reform.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is at peace and ritual and righteousness prevail. Extraordinary mercy cannot be handed out again and again, or the foolish will count on luck, break the law on purpose, and never mend their ways.

sentences.zh: 」八月甲戌朔，幸朝堂，親覽冤屈。

translations.literal: " On the first day of the eighth month, jiaxu, he went to the Court Hall and personally examined cases of wrong and injustice.
translations.idiomatic: " On jiaxu, the first day of the eighth month, he went to the main hall and heard grievances in person.

sentences.zh: 自是，上以軍國無事，每日視膳於西宮。

translations.literal: From this time on, with military and state affairs at peace, the emperor daily attended to his father's meals at the Western Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, with war and state business quiet, he went each day to the Western Palace to see that his father was served at table.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，公卿奏曰：「依禮，季夏之月，可以居臺榭。

translations.literal: On guisi the high ministers memorialized: "According to ritual, in the last month of summer one may dwell in a terrace pavilion."
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the chief ministers memorialized: "By ritual, in the last month of summer one may lodge in a raised pavilion."

sentences.zh: 今隆暑未退，秋霖方始，宮中卑濕，請營一閣以居之。

translations.literal: Now the great heat has not yet subsided and the autumn rains are just beginning; the palace is low and damp—we ask that a pavilion be built for Your Majesty to dwell in."
translations.idiomatic: "The great heat has not yet broken, and the autumn rains are only beginning. The palace stands low and damp. We beg that a pavilion be built for Your Majesty's residence."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕有氣病，豈宜下濕。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I suffer from a breathing ailment—how could I abide low dampness?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "I suffer from a breathing ailment. How could I endure such damp?"

sentences.zh: 若遂來請，糜費良多。

translations.literal: If I yielded to your repeated requests, the waste would be great."
translations.idiomatic: If I yielded to your pleas, the cost would be enormous."

sentences.zh: 昔漢文帝將起露臺，而惜十家之產。

translations.literal: In old times Emperor Wen of Han was about to build the Dew Terrace yet spared the livelihood of ten households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han once planned the Dew Terrace but stayed his hand for the sake of ten families' livelihood.

sentences.zh: 朕德不逮於漢帝，而所費過之，豈謂為民父母之道也。

translations.literal: My virtue does not match that Han emperor's, yet I would spend even more—can this be called the way of a parent to the people?"
translations.idiomatic: My virtue falls short of that Han emperor's, yet I would spend even more. Is that the conduct of a ruler who is parent to his people?"

sentences.zh: 」竟不許。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he refused.

sentences.zh: 是月，河南、河北大霜，人饑。

translations.literal: That month there was heavy frost in Henan and Hebei, and the people suffered famine.
translations.idiomatic: That month severe frost struck Henan and Hebei, and the people went hungry.

sentences.zh: 九月丙午，詔曰：「尚齒重舊，先王以之垂範；

translations.literal: On the ninth month, bingwu, an edict said: "Honoring the aged and valuing the old—former kings took this as a model left to posterity;"
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu of the ninth month he decreed: "To honor the aged and esteem the old was the example former kings left to later ages;"

sentences.zh: 還章解組，朝臣於是克終。

translations.literal: returning seals and unbinding the sash, court ministers thereby might see their duties through to the end.
translations.idiomatic: to return one's seals and lay aside office was how ministers of the court might bring their service to a worthy close.

sentences.zh: 釋菜合樂之儀，東膠西序之制，養老之義，遺文可睹。

translations.literal: The rites of offering vegetables and harmonizing music, the institutions of the eastern and western schools—the meaning of nurturing the aged can be seen in surviving texts.
translations.idiomatic: The rites of the vegetable offering and communal music, the eastern and western academies—the way of caring for the elderly still shines in the old records.

sentences.zh: 朕恭膺大寶，憲章故實，乞言尊事，彌切深衷。

translations.literal: I respectfully received the great treasure; I take the statutes and former practices as my charter; to seek words and honor affairs of state cuts to the depths of my heart.
translations.idiomatic: I have taken the throne in reverence for antiquity, govern by the ordinances of former times, and hold counsel with the elders as the core of my intent.

sentences.zh: 然情存今古，世踵澆季，而策名就列，或乖大體。

translations.literal: Yet sentiments linger between past and present; the age treads in the steps of a dissolute season; yet some who register their names and take their places in the ranks depart from the great norm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet hearts still waver between past and present, and the age follows a decadent course; some who take office and enter the ranks fall short of the larger principle.

sentences.zh: 至若筋力將盡，桑榆且迫，徒竭夙興之勤，未悟夜行之罪。

translations.literal: When their sinew and bone are nearly spent and the mulberry and setting sun press near, they exhaust dawn-to-dusk diligence yet do not perceive the fault of walking by night.
translations.idiomatic: When strength fails and evening draws on, they wear themselves out with dawn labors yet never grasp that they should have retired at dusk.

sentences.zh: 其有心驚止足，行堪激勵，謝事公門，收骸閭里，能以禮讓，固可嘉焉。

translations.literal: Those whose hearts take warning at the stopping-foot, whose conduct can serve to inspire, who resign office at the public gate and gather their bones in their hamlets, who can yield by ritual—these are indeed to be praised.
translations.idiomatic: But those who know when to stop, whose conduct may inspire others, who leave office and return home, and who yield their place with proper grace—these deserve praise.

sentences.zh: 內外文武群官年高致仕、抗表去職者，參朝之日，宜在本品見任之上。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials at court and abroad who retire on account of age, or who submit memorials resigning office—on days they attend court they should rank above those presently holding their former grade."
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials, at court or in the provinces, who retire on account of age or who submit memorials to resign—on days they attend court they shall take precedence over those currently serving in the rank they once held."

sentences.zh: 」丁未，謂侍臣曰：「婦人幽閉深宮，情實可愍。

translations.literal: " On dingwei he said to his ministers: "Women shut away in the deep palace—truly this moves pity."
translations.idiomatic: " On dingwei he told his ministers: "Women shut away in the inner palace—one cannot but pity them."

sentences.zh: 隋氏末年，求採無已，至於離宮別館，非幸御之所，多聚宮人，皆竭人財力，朕所不取。

translations.literal: In the Sui's last years recruitment knew no end; even at detached palaces and lodges where the emperor did not lodge in favor, palace women were gathered in great numbers, draining the people's wealth and strength—this I will not do.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sui's final years the court took women without cease; even at detached palaces the emperor never visited, palace women were hoarded until the people were drained of wealth and strength. I will not follow that path.

sentences.zh: 且灑掃之餘，更何所用？

translations.literal: After sweeping and dusting, what further use have they?
translations.idiomatic: Once the halls are swept, what further use are they?

sentences.zh: 今將出之，任求伉儷，非獨以惜費，亦人得各遂其性。

translations.literal: Now I will release them and let them seek husbands—not only to spare expense, but so each may fulfill her nature."
translations.idiomatic: I mean to release them and let them marry—not only to save expense, but so each may live as nature intended."

sentences.zh: 」於是遣尚書左丞戴胄、給事中杜正倫等，於掖庭宮西門簡出之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Dai Zhou, Presentation Attendant Du Zhenlun, and others to select them out at the west gate of the Rear Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Dai Zhou, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, Du Zhenlun, Presentation Attendant, and others to select them out at the west gate of the Rear Palace.

sentences.zh: 冬十月庚辰，御史大夫、安吉郡公杜淹卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on gengchen, Censor-in-Chief and Duke of Anji Du Yan died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen in the tenth winter month Du Yan, Censor-in-Chief and Duke of Anji, died.

sentences.zh: 戊子，殺瀛州刺史盧祖尚。

translations.literal: On wuzi Lu Zushang, Prefect of Yingzhou, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Lu Zushang, prefect of Yingzhou, was put to death.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛酉，有事於圓丘。

translations.literal: On xinyou there was a sacrifice at the Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou he offered sacrifice at the Circular Mound.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬午，黃門侍郎王珪為侍中。

translations.literal: On renwu Huangmen Attendant Wang Gui was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Wang Gui, Huangmen Attendant, was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年三年春正月辛亥，契丹渠帥來朝。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan, in the spring of the first month, on xinhai, a Khitan chieftain came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan, on xinhai of the first spring month, a Khitan chieftain came to court.

sentences.zh: 戊午，謁太廟。

translations.literal: On wuwu he visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu he paid visit to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，親耕籍田。

translations.literal: On guihai he personally plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai he performed the plowing rite at the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 辛未，司空、魏國公裴寂坐事免。

translations.literal: On xinwei Minister of Works and Duke of Wei Pei Ji was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Pei Ji, Minister of Works and Duke of Wei, was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 二月戊寅，中書令、邢國公房玄齡為尚書左僕射，兵部尚書、檢校侍中、蔡國公杜如晦為尚書右僕射，刑部尚書、檢校中書令、永康縣公李靖為兵部尚書，右丞魏徵為守秘書監，參預朝政。

translations.literal: On the second month, wuyin, Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Duke of Xing Fang Xuanling was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Minister of War and Acting Palace Attendant Du Ruhui, Duke of Cai, was made Right Vice Director; Minister of Punishments and Acting Chief Minister of the Secretariat Li Jing, Duke of Yongkang county, was made Minister of War; Right Assistant Director Wei Zheng was made Acting Director of the Palace Library and took part in government.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin of the second month Fang Xuanling, Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Duke of Xing, became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Du Ruhui, Minister of War and Acting Palace Attendant, Duke of Cai, became Right Vice Director; Li Jing, Minister of Punishments and Acting Chief Minister of the Secretariat, Duke of Yongkang, became Minister of War; and Wei Zheng, Right Assistant Director, became Acting Director of the Palace Library with a seat in deliberations.

sentences.zh: 夏四月辛巳，太上皇徙居大安宮。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on xinsi, the Retired Emperor moved to Da'an Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi of the fourth summer month the Retired Emperor moved to Da'an Palace.

sentences.zh: 甲子，太宗始於太極殿聽政。

translations.literal: On jiazi Taizong began to hear government at Taiji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Taizong began holding court at Taiji Hall.

sentences.zh: 五月，周王元方薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Prince of Zhou Yuanfang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Prince of Zhou, Yuanfang, died.

sentences.zh: 六月戊寅，以旱，親錄囚徒。

translations.literal: On the sixth month, wuyin, because of drought he personally reviewed prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin of the sixth month, because of drought, he personally reviewed prisoners.

sentences.zh: 遣長孫無忌、房玄齡等祈雨於名山大川，中書舍人杜正倫等往關內諸州慰撫。

translations.literal: He sent Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and others to pray for rain at famous mountains and rivers; Presentation Draftsman Du Zhenlun and others went to the Guannei circuits to comfort and reassure.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and others to pray for rain at renowned mountains and rivers; Du Zhenlun, Presentation Draftsman, and others went to the Guannei circuits to comfort the people.

sentences.zh: 又令文武官各上封事，極言得失。

translations.literal: He also ordered civil and military officials each to submit sealed memorials speaking fully of gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered civil and military officials to submit sealed memorials setting forth whatever was right or wrong in government.

sentences.zh: 已卯，大風折木。

translations.literal: On jimao a great wind broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao a violent wind snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 秋八月己巳朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month, jisi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, the first day of the eighth month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: The Xueyantuo sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo sent a tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 九月癸丑，諸州置醫學。

translations.literal: On the ninth month, guichou, medical schools were established in the prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou of the ninth month medical schools were established in the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月丙午，西突厥、高昌遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, on bingwu, the Western Turks and Gaochang sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu in the eleventh winter month the Western Turks and Gaochang sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以並州都督李世勣為通漢道行軍總管，兵部尚書李靖為定襄道行軍總管，以擊突厥。

translations.literal: On gengshen Li Shiji, Area Commander of Bingzhou, was made Overall Commander of the Tonghan Circuit army; Li Jing, Minister of War, was made Overall Commander of the Dingxiang Circuit army—to strike the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Li Shiji, commander at Bingzhou, was made overall commander on the Tonghan front and Li Jing, Minister of War, overall commander on the Dingxiang front, to campaign against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊辰，突利可汗來奔。

translations.literal: On wuchen Qaghan Tuli came in flight to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Qaghan Tuli fled to the court and submitted.

sentences.zh: 癸未，杜如晦以疾辭位，許之。

translations.literal: On guiwei Du Ruhui resigned office on account of illness; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Du Ruhui asked leave of office because of illness, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，詔

translations.literal: On guichou an edict:
translations.idiomatic: On guichou he issued an edict:

sentences.zh: 建義以來交兵之處，為義士勇夫殞身戎陣者各立一寺，命虞世南、李伯藥、褚亮、顏師古、岑文本、許敬宗、硃子奢等為之碑銘，以紀功業。

translations.literal: At every place where arms had been joined since the founding struggle, a temple was to be established for each loyal warrior who had given his life on campaign; Yu Shinan, Li Boyao, Chu Liang, Yan Shigu, Cen Wenben, Xu Jingzong, Zhu Zishe, and others were ordered to compose stele inscriptions recording their achievements.
translations.idiomatic: For every battlefield since the founding struggle, a temple was to be raised for each loyal man who fell in arms; Yu Shinan, Li Boyao, Chu Liang, Yan Shigu, Cen Wenben, Xu Jingzong, Zhu Zishe, and others were charged to write stele inscriptions commemorating their deeds.

sentences.zh: 是歲，戶部奏言：中國人自塞外來歸及突厥前後內附、開四夷為州縣者，男女一百二十餘萬口。

translations.literal: That year the Ministry of Revenue memorialized: Chinese who had returned from beyond the frontier, together with Turks who had successively submitted and the opening of the four barbarian regions as prefectures and counties, numbered more than 1,200,000 persons in all.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Ministry of Revenue reported that Chinese returning from beyond the passes, Turks who had submitted in succession, and peoples of the four frontier regions newly organized as prefectures and counties together amounted to more than 1,200,000 souls.
